title: fix: Thai/complex-script rendering (#741), host speech-voice leak (#731), WebGL↔screen coherence (#729), + Playwright 1.61 support
body:
## Related Issue

Closes #741
Closes #731
Closes #729
Closes #653 (via the cherry-picked #742)

Also resolves the investigation in #733 — see "On #733" below; no code change was needed.

## Description

Five commits, each a single logical change. One carries upstream authorship: #742 (@LamerLink). #729 builds on ideas from #730 (@dyiapanis).

**`ad697a8` — #741: perturb glyph advances only, not positioning offsets**

`anti-font-fingerprinting.patch` fed a running total into each glyph's `x_offset`/`y_offset` as well as its advance:

```cpp
glyphPositions[i].x_advance += spacing;
glyphPositions[i].x_offset  += cumulativeOffset;   // <-- bug
cumulativeOffset += spacing;
```

`x_offset` is the GPOS positioning offset — the thing that parks a combining mark over its base. It contributes nothing to the measured width, so it adds nothing to the metric the randomisation exists to perturb, but layout never sees it either: `gfxTextRun` stores advances while painting honours the offsets. The running total therefore paints every glyph a further `spacing` past where layout placed it.

Latin hides this because Gecko's word cache shapes each space-delimited word separately, so the accumulator resets constantly. **Thai has no inter-word spaces**, so a whole paragraph is one shaping run and the error grows without bound — which is why the reporter saw English render fine and Thai come out mangled. Since the seed is randomised per launch, severity is a per-run lottery, which is why it looked like a beta.28 → beta.29 regression. It isn't: fonts, fontconfig and every font patch are byte-identical between those two releases.

**`160c806` — #731: make spoofed speech voices fail closed**

`nsSynthVoiceRegistry` only withheld the host's speech-dispatcher voices when the explicit `voices:blockIfNotDefined` flag was set. Nothing set it, so the host was suppressed only as a side effect of a non-empty spoofed list — and the Python layer built that list inside a bare `except Exception: pass`. Any path leaving the list empty or unset fell through to the host backend and exposed **14805 espeak-ng voices** under a fingerprint claiming macOS or Windows.

Closed at both layers: the browser now blocks whenever MaskConfig carries a `voices` array at all (including an empty one), `launch_options` pins the flag and degrades a generation failure to `[]`, and `validate_voices` rejects the bare-string / half-filled shapes `MVoices()` silently drops. With no `voices` key the browser still behaves like stock Firefox, so a bare binary is unaffected.

**`d6a806e` — #729: keep the WebGL renderer coherent with the screen**

The premise of a GPU↔screen lookup table has to survive one fact: **Firefox never reports the GPU it sees.** `dom/canvas/SanitizeRenderer.cpp` collapses every renderer string into one of ~11 representative device buckets before a page sees it — prefs `webgl.sanitize-unmasked-renderer` and `webgl.enable-renderer-query`, both default `true`; `resistFingerprinting` replaces the value with `"Mozilla"` outright. That file's own header comment gives the flavour:

> Narrow renderer string space down to representative replacements. E.g. `"GeForce RTX 3090"` => `"GeForce GTX 980"`

Two consequences drive the implementation.

*Raw model names can never match.* Every RTX, every Quadro M/P/V/T and every GeForce 900–7999 arrive as one string; `Intel(R) UHD Graphics 620` and `Mesa Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics` arrive as `Intel(R) HD Graphics` spellings. A table keyed on RTX / Quadro / RX / UHD / Iris / Mesa Intel matches nothing in `webgl_data.db` — all 33 rows are sanitized bucket strings. So renderers are reduced to their bucket first (`_renderer_bucket`), which also puts the ANGLE, nouveau and `/PCIe/SSE2` spellings of one GPU on one rule instead of three: the DB carries both `NVIDIA GeForce GTX 980, or similar` (proprietary driver) and `GeForce GTX 980, or similar` (nouveau, which loses the vendor prefix), and both must classify alike.

*A bucket carries almost no screen floor.* `GeForce GTX 980, or similar` is what a mobile GTX 1650 Max-Q reports, and `Radeon R9 200 Series, or similar` is what a Vega 8 budget laptop reports. 1366x768 laptops with discrete GPUs are ordinary hardware. The only claim true of *every* part behind a bucket is that discrete GPUs did not ship in netbooks, so that is the only claim encoded: the four discrete buckets require a screen larger than 1024x600. It is an **area**, not a width×height pair, because real panels do not dominate one another — 1280x800 and 1366x768 are both ordinary, and a per-axis floor taken from either rejects the other.

Three further properties:

- **Software rasterizers keep their natural rate.** A plain reject loop renormalises the surviving pool onto `llvmpipe` / WARP / SwiftShader; on a sub-floor screen that turns a 1.5% software rate into ~40% — trading a weak incoherence for the strongest VM/headless tell there is. So the first draw settles hardware-vs-software at the pool's own rate and is never resampled; rejection only ever runs within the hardware class.
- **Both entry points get the same treatment.** `generate_context_fingerprint()` — the per-context API #729's proposed solution names, and the one build-tester drives the browser through — sampled with a bare `sample_webgl()` and applied no floor. It now matches `launch_options()`.
- **Presets are never rewritten.** `raise_screen_to_modern_floor` lifts netbook-era BrowserForge geometry, but `_user_set_screen_window` is computed before a preset merges into the config, so the floor was rewriting real preset screens. Two bundled v150 presets genuinely report 736x414 and 960x540; both were being forced to 1366x768, breaking the very coherence #729 is about. The floor is now gated to synthetic draws.

From #730 (@dyiapanis): constrain the GPU to the screen rather than the screen to the GPU, so rejection sampling preserves `webgl_data.db`'s real OS weighting and leaves the already-reconciled geometry alone (#499); measure the screen-to-avail gap *before* mutating (#730 computed it after overwriting `screen.height`, turning a 1024x600 → 1080 bump into a 520px "taskbar"); and no Apple-M Retina floor, since Apple silicon also ships in the Mac mini and Mac Studio driving arbitrary external displays.

**`2b662a8` — Playwright 1.61+ support** (cherry-picked from #742 by @LamerLink, unmodified)

Included because the Playwright suite could not run at all without it — 1.62 produced 377 fixture errors, so this branch was untestable against current Playwright. Verified here (see below); #742 itself carried no test results.

**`17f873a` — bound the Playwright range instead of unpinning it**

#742 replaced `playwright = "<1.61"` with `"*"`. The breakage it fixes is real, but an unbounded range removes the tripwire rather than making the browser forward-compatible: `camoufox.server` imports `playwright._impl._driver.compute_driver_executable`, a private API with no compat guarantee, and `additions/juggler` is a fork of one Playwright vintage that every minor release is free to break again — 1.61 sending `viewport.isMobile` is exactly that, and it will recur. So the cap moves up to the tested-current 1.62.0 rather than away. No lower bound is added; this package has never carried one. `build-tester/requirements.txt` mirrors this pin by its own comment and moves with it.

Kept as a separate commit so the cherry-pick stays byte-identical to @LamerLink's — reading commit-by-commit, the pin therefore goes `<1.61` → `*` → `<1.63`.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Other

## Testing

Linux x86_64, built from this branch's own patch files (0 failed hunks). The built juggler in `dist/` is byte-identical to `additions/juggler/`, so the tested binary carries this branch.

**Before / after, measured on the built binary:**

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| #741 Thai painted-text overrun past its layout box (1x / 2x / 4x run length) | +4.90 / +9.80 / +20.60 px | **0.00 / 0.00 / 0.00 px** |
| #741 same measurement, Latin | 0.00 px | 0.00 px |
| #741 width perturbation (the actual fingerprinting signal) | 4 / 8 / 16 / 32 px | **unchanged** |
| #731 host voices exposed via `{"voices": []}` | 14805 | **0** |
| #731 host voices when generation raises | 14805 | **0** |
| #731 normal path | 115 | 115 |

**#729, 250 profiles per OS per entry point:**

| path | incoherent GPU/screen | min screen | software-renderer rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| `launch_options` win / mac / lin | 0 / 0 / 0 | 1600x900 / 1366x768 / 1440x900 | 1.2% / 0% / 12.4% |
| `generate_context_fingerprint` win / mac / lin | 0 / 0 / 0 | 1376x774 / 1366x768 / 1440x900 | 1.2% / 0% / 9.2% |

Software rates sit at the pool's natural baseline (1.5% win, 9.0% lin) within sampling noise — the constraint does not reweight the pool. Both sub-netbook v150 presets round-trip unchanged (736x414, 960x540).

Where the constraint actually binds is worth stating plainly: on the **default synthetic path it is a no-op**, because the netbook floor already guarantees ≥1366x768 and no discrete-GPU/netbook pair is reachable. It earns its place when the floor is skipped (user-pinned `screen.*`) or undone (headful on a genuinely small monitor):

| user-pinned 1024x600 | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| incoherent pairs, Windows | 52.2% | **0.0%** |
| incoherent pairs, Linux | 37.5% | **0.0%** |
| software-renderer rate, Windows | 2.00% | 2.25% |
| software-renderer rate, Linux | 9.55% | 10.10% |

**Playwright suite (`make tests`, under Xvfb)**

| binary | Playwright | result |
|---|---|---|
| stock beta.29 | 1.60 | 63 failed / 1033 passed |
| this branch (pre-#742) | 1.60 | 62 failed / 1034 passed |
| this branch (with #742) | 1.62.0 | **65 failed / 1031 passed / 107 skipped**, 0 fixture errors |
| stock or pre-#742 binary | 1.62.0 | **377 fixture errors** — suite cannot run |

NOTE: These failures are a result of the world isolation feature conflicting with the Playwright test suite, not real errors.

A display is required for a clean run: without one, the 7 `async/test_headful.py` tests fail purely for want of an X server (72 failed / 1024 passed), and they all pass under `xvfb-run`.

Set-difference against the stock baseline on 1.60: **0 failures unique to this branch.** All 62 also fail on stock beta.29; the baseline had one extra flaky one (`test_should_report_if_request_was_from_service_worker`).

The three extra failures on 1.62 were isolated to Playwright itself, not #742 — holding Playwright at 1.60 and varying only the binary, the +#742 build passes **6/6 websocket tests** and gives byte-identical tracing/network results to the pre-#742 build (same 2 failed / 60 passed, same test names). This matters because #742 makes `timestamp` a *required* protocol field on `webSocketFrameSent`/`webSocketFrameReceived`.

`pythonlib`: **156 passed**, including `tests/test_webgl_screen_consistency.py` (bucket reduction, the area floor, software-class preservation, both entry points, preset preservation) and fail-closed cases in `tests/test_voices.py`.

**Note on the uniqueness checks in the certificate below:** these flap run to run and fail on stock beta.29 too (observed 4/4, 3/4 and 2/4 on the same binary). Measured over 1500 trials, the chance that 3 generated profiles share a screen is **46.6% on Linux / 26.9% on macOS — identical with and without the change in `d6a806e`**. It is BrowserForge's 8-value screen pool, not a regression here. The screen floor is a no-op for the Linux and Windows pools (0/400 draws below it) and fires on 3.5% of macOS draws.

The reporter's own data inverts their conclusion: their leaky run used **150.0.2-alpha.26** and the clean one beta.29. title: Camoufox crashes with SIGSEGV under gVisor sandboxes — wasm_rt_syscall_set_segue_base / ARCH_SET_GS unsupported
body:
## Summary

Camoufox crashes with `SIGSEGV` a few seconds after launch when run inside a
[gVisor](https://gvisor.dev/)-sandboxed container (e.g. [Modal](https://modal.com/)
functions, Google Cloud Run, GKE Sandbox/GKE Autopilot). The crash is not
specific to Camoufox's own code — it's Firefox 136+'s WASM sandbox
(RLBox/wasm2c) requiring `arch_prctl(ARCH_SET_GS, ...)`, a syscall gVisor
does not implement ([google/gvisor#11567](https://github.com/google/gvisor/issues/11567)).
Filing here since Camoufox pins/ships that Firefox base and this will bite
anyone trying to deploy Camoufox on gVisor-backed serverless platforms.

## Environment

- camoufox-js: `0.12.0`
- playwright: `1.60.0`
- Base image: `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.60.0-noble`
- Host: Modal (gVisor-sandboxed container runtime), x86_64
- Launch options: `{ headless: true, geoip: true }` via `launchOptions()` from `camoufox-js`

## Repro

```js
import { launchOptions } from 'camoufox-js';
import { firefox } from 'playwright';

const opts = await launchOptions({ headless: true, geoip: true });
const browser = await firefox.launch(opts);
browser.on('disconnected', () => console.log('disconnected'));
// crashes within ~3s of launch, before any page is opened
```

## Observed (with `DEBUG=pw:browser`)

```
pw:browser <launching> /opt/camoufox/camoufox-bin -no-remote -headless -profile ... -juggler-pipe -silent
pw:browser <launched> pid=38
pw:browser [pid=38][err] *** You are running in headless mode.
pw:browser [pid=38][out] [GFX1-]: FireTestProcess failed: Failed to spawn child process "/opt/camoufox/glxtest" (No such file or directory)
pw:browser [pid=38][err] JavaScript warning: resource://services-settings/Utils.sys.mjs, line 119: unreachable code after return statement
pw:browser [pid=38][out] Juggler listening to the pipe
pw:browser [pid=38][err] wasm_rt_syscall_set_segue_base error: Invalid argument
pw:browser [pid=38][err] Redirecting call to abort() to mozalloc_abort
pw:browser [pid=38] <process did exit: exitCode=null, signal=SIGSEGV>
```

## What I tried

- Setting `MOZ_DISABLE_CONTENT_SANDBOX=1` in the launched process's env
  (confirmed via `opts.env.MOZ_DISABLE_CONTENT_SANDBOX` that it does reach
  the child process) — no effect. This makes sense in hindsight: this is
  the WASM/RLBox sandbox, not the OS-level content-process sandbox that env
  var controls.
- No firefox_user_pref or launch arg found that disables the WASM
  segue-based sandboxing at runtime.

## Question / ask

Is there a supported way to disable the WASM segue optimization (or the
RLBox-sandboxed libraries that trigger it) at runtime or launch-option time,
so Camoufox can run under gVisor-based sandboxes until gVisor implements
`ARCH_SET_GS`? If there's a Firefox pref or build flag for this already,
happy to test and report back — a `launchOptions()` flag would make this a
clean workaround for anyone deploying to gVisor-backed platforms (Modal,
Cloud Run, GKE Sandbox).

Reference: https://github.com/google/gvisor/issues/11567

title: macOS: headed Camoufox activates itself (steals key/mouse focus) at window show — even with Playwright's '-foreground' launch flag removed
body:
### Describe the bug

On macOS, every headed Camoufox launch brings its window to the very front and takes keyboard AND mouse focus from whatever app the user is working in. This makes unattended automation on a machine someone is actively using very painful (we run one fresh Camoufox per scraped URL — each launch interrupts the user).

We isolated it past the usual suspect: Playwright's Firefox launcher normally passes the '-foreground' CLI flag (launch-time activation). We removed it via `ignore_default_args=["-foreground"]` (passed through camoufox's launch_options to firefox.launch) and verified via `ps` that the real spawned process runs WITHOUT it:

```
camoufox -no-remote -wait-for-browser -profile <tmp> -juggler-pipe -silent
```

The focus steal still happens — but NOT at launch: measured with a 0.25s AppleScript poll of AXMain on the Camoufox process, the window becomes key at ~t=3.6s and STAYS key for ~3s, which lines up with browser-window creation/first show (new_page/goto), not process start. So something in the window-show path performs an explicit self-activation.

For comparison, the Playwright team states (microsoft/playwright#41306) that stock headed Firefox no longer steals focus once '-foreground' is dropped — so this looks specific to the Camoufox build (window sizing/positioning patches or theming performing an explicit raise/activate on show?).

An `LSUIElement=true` Info.plist patch on the .app bundle does not help either — consistent with an explicit activation call overriding the passive accessory policy (the Dock icon also still appears on these direct-binary launches).

### To Reproduce

```python
from camoufox.async_api import AsyncCamoufox
# ignore_default_args passes through to playwright.firefox.launch
async with AsyncCamoufox(headless=False, os="macos", ignore_default_args=["-foreground"]) as browser:
    page = await browser.new_page()
    await page.goto("https://example.com")
```
Focus another app before the window appears — Camoufox raises itself above it and takes key focus at window show.

### Expected

A way to launch headed Camoufox on macOS without it activating itself — e.g. respect the '-foreground'-absent launch by not self-activating on first window show, or a config/pref to suppress the raise (the analog of what makes stock headed Firefox background-friendly).

### Environment
- Camoufox 152.0.4-beta.28 (official, ~/Library/Caches/camoufox), python lib via Playwright bundled driver
- macOS arm64
- Workaround we run today: an external watchdog that re-activates the previously focused app whenever Camoufox becomes key — bounds the steal to a sub-second flicker, but a real fix needs to be in the browser.

title: add_init_script() no longer reaches the page world in beta.29, silently
body:
### Describe the bug:

Since the isolated-world change in #707, `add_init_script()` only ever patches the isolated world. Any script installed that way — fingerprint spoofing, API patching, anything meant for the site — stops reaching page script.

`page.evaluate()` has the `mw:` escape hatch for this. Init scripts do not, and the two facts together make the failure silent.

Measured on the shipped `152.0.4-beta.29` Linux x86_64 build, A/B'd against `152.0.4-beta.28` on the same machine. The probe is a page served over local HTTP that hashes its own canvas from an inline `<script>` and writes the result to `document.title` — i.e. it measures what a *site* sees, not what automation sees.

| | init script reaches the page | profile A | profile B | A with no script |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| beta.28 | yes | `935f6c78` | `528b6cdb` | `5bf14e69` |
| beta.29 | **no** | `5bf14e69` | `5bf14e69` | `5bf14e69` |

Under beta.29 all three readings collapse onto the host's own rendering. Two profiles with different noise seeds hand a site the identical canvas.

Three things make this worse than a plain regression:

1. **The usual probe cannot see it.** Reading the same value back through `page.evaluate()` still returns two different, properly noised hashes — that is the world the init script landed in. Our browser test suite passed in full on a build that had stopped spoofing anything a site could observe.
2. **`mw:` in an init script is silently accepted.** Playwright wraps every `add_init_script` body in `(() => { ... })()`, so the prefix ends up *inside* the wrapper, where it parses as a label statement. No error, no effect.
3. **It is the failure mode a spoofing tool can least afford.** Nothing downstream can tell. Init scripts reach `ExecutionContext.evaluateScriptSafely()` (`FrameTree.js:660`), whose `catch` writes to `dump()` and returns — so even a throwing script surfaces nothing to the client. There is no exception, no warning, and every automation-side check keeps reporting success.

I'd suggest either wiring `mw:` through the init-script path, or — if init scripts are meant to stay isolated by design — rejecting the prefix loudly there, so it fails at call time instead of silently.

Adjacent but not the same: #733 reports globals leaking *into* the main world in 0.6.0. This is the opposite direction.

### Screenshots:

Not applicable — the measurements are in the table above.

### To Reproduce:

Serve a page that hashes its canvas in an inline `<script>` and writes it to `document.title`:

```html
<!doctype html><meta charset="utf-8"><body><script>
  const h = (t) => { let x = 5381;
    for (let i = 0; i < t.length; i++) x = ((x * 33) ^ t.charCodeAt(i)) >>> 0;
    return x.toString(16); };
  const c = document.createElement('canvas'); c.width = 200; c.height = 50;
  const x = c.getContext('2d'); x.textBaseline = 'top'; x.font = '14px Arial';
  x.fillStyle = '#f60'; x.fillRect(0, 0, 100, 25);
  x.fillStyle = '#069'; x.fillText('probe', 2, 15);
  document.title = h(c.toDataURL()) + '|' + (window.__marker || 'absent');
</script></body>
```

Then:

```python
from camoufox.sync_api import NewBrowser
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

with sync_playwright() as pw:
    ctx = NewBrowser(pw, from_options=options, persistent_context=True)
    ctx.add_init_script("window.__marker = 'present';")   # plus any canvas patch
    page = ctx.new_page()
    page.goto(url, wait_until="load")
    print(page.title())
```

On beta.28 the title reports `present`. On beta.29 it reports `absent`, and the canvas hash is the host's, unchanged by whatever the init script did.

Prefixing the init script with `"mw:"` changes nothing either way, with or without `main_world_eval=True`.

<details>
<summary>What I tried, and why I am not sending it as a PR</summary>

`evaluateScriptSafely()` is the only path init scripts take — `FrameTree.js:660` runs it over `world._scriptsToEvaluateOnNewDocument`, per world, on `_onGlobalObjectCleared`. Teaching it the prefix — allowing for Playwright's wrapper — does restore the behaviour: the same probe then reads two distinct noised hashes.

The default world is the right place for it: `_createIsolatedContext()` gives its twin only to the unnamed world (`FrameTree.js:594`), which is exactly the one init scripts land in.

But it is **not reliable**. Over eight consecutive launches, two still rendered the host canvas. Same code, same profile: a race, not a logic error.

`mainWorldContext()` builds its `ExecutionContext` lazily from `_mainWorldGlobal`, which `_createIsolatedContext()` sets from `this.domWindow()`. When init scripts run, that global is occasionally not the one the document ends up with, and `executeInGlobal` either throws (swallowed by the surrounding `catch`) or writes into a global nobody reads.

Building the main-world twin eagerly, alongside the default world in `_createIsolatedContext()`, would tie it to the right document. I did not send that as a patch because the lazy build is commented as deliberate ("keeps the page's own global out of the debuggee set entirely for sessions that never use `mw:`"), and I cannot tell what eager creation costs elsewhere. That call is yours.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Workaround, for anyone hitting this</summary>

A content script declared in the main world does not go through Juggler at all, and works identically on both versions. Load it as a temporary extension:

```json
{
  "manifest_version": 3,
  "name": "spoof",
  "version": "1.0",
  "browser_specific_settings": { "gecko": { "id": "spoof@example" } },
  "content_scripts": [{
    "matches": ["<all_urls>"],
    "js": ["spoof.js"],
    "run_at": "document_start",
    "all_frames": true,
    "world": "MAIN",
    "match_about_blank": true,
    "match_origin_as_fallback": true
  }]
}
```

then pass its directory via `addons=[...]`.

`match_about_blank` and `match_origin_as_fallback` matter: without them the inherited frames (`about:blank`, `blob:`, `srcdoc`) are missed, which is worse than no spoofing — the parent page is patched and the child frame is not.

Measured page-side under beta.29, this adds no observable surface: no extra own-property on `window`, `chrome` and `browser` both still `undefined`, `toDataURL.toString()` still `[native code]`. No `web_accessible_resources` is declared, which is what would expose the extension's internal UUID to the page.

</details>

### Version:

```
Python Packages
  Camoufox                    v0.5.5
  Browserforge                v1.2.4
  Apify Fingerprints          v0.15.0
  Playwright                  v1.60.0
Browser
  Camoufox                    v152.0.4-beta.29 (also tested against beta.28)
```

Linux x86_64.

title: Search service fails to initialize: bundled `search-config-overrides-v2` dump is missing `recordType`
body:
## Summary

`SearchService.#init()` throws on every launch, on a clean profile, in both
`152.0.4-beta.28` and `152.0.4-beta.29`. The browser ends up with **no search
engines at all**, and — because the urlbar's heuristic result depends on the
search service — the address bar drop-down shows **nothing**: no history, no
autofill, no bookmarks. Typing a word navigates to it as a hostname instead.

## Error

```
console.debug: SearchService: "init"
console.error: SearchService: "#init: failure initializing search:"
    (new Error("reason: JSON error: missing field `recordType` at line 1 column 114",
     "moz-src:///toolkit/components/uniffi-bindgen-gecko-js/components/generated/RustSearch.sys.mjs", 2681))
```

## Cause

The bundled Remote Settings dump

```
omni.ja → defaults/settings/main/search-config-overrides-v2.json
```

holds one record whose keys are:

```
clickUrl, id, identifier, last_modified, partnerCode, schema, telemetrySuffix, urls
```

There is no `recordType`, which the Rust `SearchEngineSelector` requires. For
comparison, every one of the 157 records in the sibling `search-config-v2.json`
does carry `recordType`, so only the overrides dump is stale.

## Steps to reproduce

```bash
camoufox fetch official/152.0.4-beta.29
# fresh profile, search logging on
printf 'user_pref("browser.search.log", true);\n' > /tmp/prof/user.js
camoufox -profile /tmp/prof -headless -no-remote about:blank
```

The error appears within a second of startup. `search.json.mozlz4` is never
written, and the profile has no engines.

## Impact

- No search from the address bar; a typed word is treated as a hostname.
- The urlbar drop-down is empty — history and autofill are unreachable even
  though `places.sqlite` is populated and `browser.urlbar.suggest.history` is
  `true`. All urlbar providers register fine (`UrlbarProviderPlaces`,
  `UrlbarProviderAutofill`, `UrlbarProviderHeuristicFallback`); the results just
  never get built.
- Adding an engine through `policies.json` (`SearchEngines.Add`) does not help,
  and neither does a WebExtension declaring `chrome_settings_overrides.
  search_provider` — both register through the same dead service.

## Suggested fix

Refresh the bundled `search-config-overrides-v2.json` from Remote Settings so
its record carries `recordType`, or ship `{"data": []}` — the overrides
collection is optional, and an empty one lets the service start.

Locally, replacing that file inside `omni.ja` with `{"data": []}` is the only
workaround we found, and it is lost on every browser update.

## Environment

- Camoufox `152.0.4-beta.28` and `152.0.4-beta.29`, Windows x86_64
- Clean profile, no policies, no extensions

title: feat: derive period-correct navigator.buildID when not explicitly set
body:
## Summary

Distributed Camoufox binaries carry their own engine `buildID`, and unless a user explicitly sets `navigator.buildID`, Firefox's XULAppInfo reports it verbatim. This lets a modern Firefox UA claim a years-old build (observed: UA `Firefox/152.0` with buildID `20181001000000`, i.e. a Firefox 63-era timestamp) — a trivially cross-checkable inconsistency that fingerprint detectors actively test for.

This PR defaults `navigator.buildID` to a period-correct value derived from the claimed major version when the user has not set one explicitly.

## Changes

- `_default_build_id(ff_version)` — deterministic YYYYMMDDHHMMSS within the plausible release window of the claimed Firefox major version (anchored to Firefox 94 = Nov 2021, ~4 weeks per subsequent release, stable jitter per version so the same version always yields the same ID).
- `_ff_major_from_ua(ua)` — fallback that extracts the major version from the generated UA when `ff_version` is not passed.
- Both wired into `generate_context_fingerprint()` via the same `setdefault` pattern already used for `fonts` / `voices` / `oscpu`, so both the preset and BrowserForge paths are covered.

Users who set `navigator.buildID` explicitly are completely unaffected.

## Testing

```
cd pythonlib && python -m pytest tests/test_default_build_id.py -v
# 10 passed
python -m pytest tests/ -q
# 118 passed (no regressions)
```

New tests cover: 14-digit format, determinism, monotonicity across versions (newer majors never map to earlier dates), period plausibility for modern versions, explicit-value preservation, and integration through `generate_context_fingerprint`.

title: Headed mode on Windows: visual artifacts and stale rendering when resizing the window during interactive use
body:
## User experience

A human operator drives a headed Camoufox window interactively (manual login flows, OAuth consent screens). While resizing the OS window, the right-hand side of the viewport shows persistent rendering artifacts, and page content intermittently fails to redraw after navigation or redirect — the page appears stalled until another interaction forces a repaint. The workflow breaks because the operator cannot trust what is rendered while adjusting the window mid-flow.

Observed on Windows 10 (10.0.26100), Camoufox v0.5.5 (Python package), browser build official/stable v152.0.4-beta.28 (Firefox 152), launched with `headless=False, humanize=True` via `sync_api`.

## Reproduction

1. Launch a headed session:
   ```python
   from camoufox.sync_api import Camoufox
   with Camoufox(headless=False, humanize=True) as browser:
       page = browser.new_page()
       page.goto("https://vercel.com/login", wait_until="domcontentloaded")
       input()  # keep window open; resize it by dragging edges now
   ```
2. Drag-resize the window repeatedly by its right edge.
3. Observe artifacts along the resized edge; then navigate to a URL that redirects (e.g. an OAuth provider) and watch whether the new page paints without further input.

## Expected behavior

Resizing repaints cleanly with no residual artifacts, and navigations/redirects paint the new document promptly without requiring additional user input.

## Actual behavior

- Stale pixels / torn strips remain visible along the right-hand side of the viewport while dragging to resize.
- After redirects (observed crossing from vercel.com into accounts.google.com), the interstitial sometimes does not paint; content appears frozen until a subsequent event triggers compositing.

## Impact

Any headed, human-in-the-loop flow (OAuth logins, consent screens) on Windows is affected. Headless automation does not surface this because there is no interactive resize. Current workaround: avoid resizing mid-flow, or relaunch; forcing software WebRender (`gfx.webrender.software=true`) is expected to mitigate but trades CPU for GPU compositing.

## Source references

This matches a long-standing class of Firefox WebRender compositor bugs on Windows:
- [Bugzilla #1578330](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1578330) — "[Windows] Glitches when resizing browser window with WebRender"; root cause was `GetBufferSize()` being called after `BeginFrame()` in `RenderCompositorANGLE`, mutating the buffer size mid-frame.
- [Bugzilla #1626116](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1626116) — stretched content when resizing under ANGLE-related WebRender paths on Windows.
- [Bugzilla #2027221](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2027221) — WebRender compositor defect in Firefox 149 (dirty-rect/device-size handling), fixed in Firefox ~150; Camoufox v152 should include that specific fix, which suggests either a regression in the 152 line or an interaction with Camoufox's patched build.

Relevant Camoufox-side code paths (hypothesis only): window sizing/viewport sync logic around [`pythonlib/camoufox/utils.py`](https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/blob/dbd511b962/pythonlib/camoufox/utils.py) (launch options → Firefox window args) and the addons that patch window/screen dimensions at [`pythonlib/camoufox/addons/`](https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/blob/dbd511b962/pythonlib/camoufox/addons/). The spoofed screen-size injection may interact badly with real OS resize events in headed mode.

## Suggested acceptance criteria

- Drag-resizing a headed window on Windows 10/11 leaves no stale strips or torn regions.
- A cross-origin redirect in a headed window paints the new document within normal frame timing without requiring extra input.
- Regression check: repeat the repro above on integrated and discrete GPUs.

## Related

- #192 — window size incorrect with persistent context (related sizing behavior, different symptom: wrong initial size rather than live-resize artifacts)
- #118, #532, #348 — earlier window-size reports
- #514 — Windows-specific graphics-stack findings (ANGLE/GPU strings) that motivated looking at the compositor path

title: Playwright globals leak into the page's main world in 0.6.0 (detected by hcaptcha)
body:
With cloverlabs-camoufox[geoip]==0.6.0, Playwright identifiers are visible on window in the page's main world, where any page script can enumerate them. Upstream camoufox==0.4.11 exposes none.

Repro (a <script> tag always runs in the main world, so it measures what the page sees regardless of which world page.evaluate targets):

from camoufox.sync_api import Camoufox

SNIPPET = """
  const n = Object.getOwnPropertyNames(window);
  document.title = JSON.stringify(n.filter(k => /playwright|pwInit|puppeteer|juggler|cdc_/i.test(k)));
"""

with Camoufox(headless=True) as browser:
    page = browser.new_page()
    page.goto("https://example.com")
    page.add_script_tag(content=SNIPPET)
    print(page.title())


Two separate things: __pwInitScripts / __playwright_builtins__ look new in Playwright 1.52 (stripping predates them), while __playwright__binding__ is hidden by 0.4.11 and not by 0.6.0 — a regression independent of the driver.

Impact: trivially detectable by Object.getOwnPropertyNames(window) scans. On an hCaptcha-protected workload, 0.4.11 + pw1.49.1 got 19/20 tokens accepted; 0.6.0 + pw1.52 got 3/20, same sites and network, alternating runs. Linux, headless, no proxy/addons/custom prefs; note the clean run used the newer browser build (152.0.4-beta.29 vs 150.0.2-alpha.26), so it isn't a browser-version effect.

Secondary: main_world_eval appears to be a no-op on 0.6.0 — page.evaluate sees 951 window properties either way, vs 77 (isolated world) on 0.4.11.

title: Bump release to beta.29
body:
Refs #707.

One line: `release=beta.28` -> `beta.29` in `upstream.sh`.

## Why

#707 changed the browser binary, not just the Python launcher — 16 of its 64 files are baked into the build:

| Where | What |
|---|---|
| `patches/` (3) | `debugger-invisible-to-content` (new, SpiderMonkey), `trusted-automation-events` (new, DOM), extended `screen-spoofing` |
| `additions/juggler/` (8) | packed into `omni.ja` — isolated-world evaluate, screencast, header order, mousemove deadlock |
| `settings/` (3) | `camoufox.cfg` (`history.length`, network partitioning), `properties.json`, `camoucfg.jvv` |
| `assets/*.mozconfig` (2) | `--enable-bundled-fonts` (macOS, #706), `--disable-debug-symbols` |

None of it reaches users until a rebuild. `--enable-bundled-fonts` in particular is a pure build flag — the macOS font fix is inert on every existing binary.

## Why the bump has to land before the tag

`Makefile` line 1-2 is `include upstream.sh` + `export`, and nothing in the build reads the git tag. Artifact filenames come from this file; the Release name comes from the tag. Tagging `v152.0.4-beta.29` without this commit would publish a release full of `camoufox-152.0.4-beta.28-*` files — colliding by name with the beta.28 already published from 0583c3e, but differing in content.

## After merge

`build.yml` triggers only on `workflow_dispatch` and `push: tags`, so merging this starts nothing. The build is started by tagging the merge commit:

```
git tag v152.0.4-beta.29 <merge-commit>
git push origin v152.0.4-beta.29
```

That runs the 6-target matrix and drafts a prerelease (`draft: true, prerelease: true`), so publishing stays a manual step.

Separately, the `pythonlib/` changes from #707 are not on PyPI either — 0.5.5 was published 2026-08-18, before that merge. Those need their own version bump plus a `publish-pypi.yml` dispatch.

title: Python voices config does not match browser schema and exposes host voices
body:
The Python wrapper emits `voices` as strings, but Camoufox browser `v152.0.4-beta.28` expects complete voice objects. The browser skips the string entries and can expose the Linux host's native voices.

Related fingerprint-coherence discussion: https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/issues/729

## Environment

- Camoufox browser `v152.0.4-beta.28`
- `cloverlabs-camoufox==0.6.0`
- BrowserForge `1.2.4`
- Headed browser under Xvfb
- Linux host

## Python behavior

The bundled `voices.json` entries use a `Name:locale:type` representation.

The Python wrapper:

1. Loads those entries.
2. Keeps only the name.
3. Generates `List[str]`.
4. Places that list in `config["voices"]`.

The fallback path can place the original string records in the same property. Therefore, one property can receive two string formats.

The browser's `properties.json` declares only:

```json
{ "property": "voices", "type": "array" }
```

The Python validator checks that the value is a list. It cannot validate the element schema.

## Browser behavior

The browser source for this build requires every `voices` element to contain:

```json
{
  "lang": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "voiceUri": "string",
  "isDefault": true,
  "isLocalService": true
}
```

The parser skips a bare string or an incomplete object.

The build also supports:

```text
voices:blockIfNotDefined
```

When that option is false or absent, native host voices can still register.

## Reproduction

A bundled macOS real-device preset was launched on a Linux host.

With the wrapper-generated string configuration:

- The configured entries were skipped.
- `speechSynthesis.getVoices()` exposed 14,805 host Linux voices.

With structured objects and `voices:blockIfNotDefined=true`:

- The browser exposed only the intended configured voices.
- The host voice leak was removed.

No voice names, IP addresses, proxy details, or private infrastructure values are included here.

A Python-only shape check also demonstrates the mismatch:

```python
config = from_preset(preset, "152")
assert isinstance(config["voices"], list)
assert all(isinstance(voice, str) for voice in config["voices"])
```

## Expected behavior

- The Python package and browser must use one documented voice element schema.
- The Python package must preserve the locale and voice type needed to build that schema.
- Invalid elements must fail validation before browser launch.
- The browser must define whether an empty configured list blocks or permits native voices.
- A valid configured list must not expose unconfigured host voices.
- Wrapper/browser compatibility data must prevent installation of a pair with incompatible configuration schemas.

## Suggested acceptance criteria

- `from_preset` emits the documented voice object format.
- Every object contains `lang`, `name`, `voiceUri`, `isDefault`, and `isLocalService`.
- Element-level validation rejects strings and incomplete objects.
- A Linux-hosted browser using a macOS preset exposes no Linux host voices.
- Tests cover a valid list, an invalid string, an incomplete object, and an empty list.
- The expected interaction with `voices:blockIfNotDefined` is documented and tested.
- The supported Python-package/browser matrix includes the configuration-schema version.

This issue is separate from #729 because it has a specific type mismatch, reproduction, and acceptance boundary. The two issues are related because the leaked host voices make the resulting device profile internally inconsistent.

title: fix: WebGL ↔ screen resolution consistency for synthetic fingerprints
body:
## Related Issue

Closes #729

## Description

When using BrowserForge synthetic fingerprint generation (the default path in `generate_context_fingerprint()`), the WebGL vendor/renderer is sampled from `webgl_data.db` independently of the BrowserForge screen resolution. This creates fingerprints where the GPU and screen resolution combination never exists on real hardware — e.g., an NVIDIA GTX 980 (high-end discrete desktop GPU) paired with a 1024x600 screen. Fingerprint consistency detectors (Pixelscan, Fingerprint.com) flag these as "masking."

**Evidence:** Running Camoufox v152.0.4-beta.28 (headed via Xvfb, no proxy) against Pixelscan's fingerprint check — browser integrity, location, proxy, and bot detection all pass, but "Fingerprint: Masking detected" fails with "Your Browser Fingerprint is inconsistent."

This PR adds `fix_webgl_screen_consistency()`, which:
1. Maps GPU classes to their typical minimum screen resolutions (e.g., NVIDIA GTX → 1920x1080, Intel HD → 1366x768, Apple M → 2560x1600)
2. If the screen resolution falls below the GPU's floor, bumps it upward to the minimum
3. Scales `availWidth/Height` and `window.outer/innerWidth/Height` proportionally, preserving the taskbar gap

This follows the same pattern as the existing consistency fixes (`fix_navigator_arch`, `fix_screen_no_taskbar`, `clamp_window_dimensions`) — all Python-only validations in `fingerprints.py`, wired into the config build in `utils.py`. Only affects the BrowserForge synthetic path; real fingerprint presets are already internally consistent.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Testing

- Python syntax verified via `ast.parse()` on both modified files
- `fix_webgl_screen_consistency()` only adjusts upward (never shrinks), preserving downstream window/viewport geometry
- Existing consistency fixes (`fix_screen_no_taskbar`, `clamp_window_dimensions`) run before this function; this function respects their established taskbar gap
- Unknown GPU renderers are skipped (no over-constraining)

## Fingerprint Report

This PR touches only the Python config layer (`pythonlib/camoufox/fingerprints.py`, `pythonlib/camoufox/utils.py`) — no C++/browser patches, no WebGL spoofing changes, no font/canvas/audio spoofing. The build-tester (which tests the raw binary with manually injected fingerprints) is N/A: the function operates on the config dict before injection, not on the browser's spoofing behavior. The service-tester would validate the end-to-end fingerprint consistency improvement.

The screen resolution adjustment is a config-layer change — `screen.width`/`screen.height` are controlled by the spoofing init script, not by the browser's display surface. The browser faithfully reports whatever the config dict injects.

title: Fingerprint cross-property inconsistency — synthetic BrowserForge fingerprints detectable as masking
body:
### Describe the bug:

When using BrowserForge synthetic fingerprint generation (the default path in `generate_context_fingerprint()`), individual fingerprint properties are generated independently — BrowserForge provides navigator/screen, then fonts, voices, WebGL vendor/renderer, and seeds are added separately. This creates fingerprints where the combination of properties never exists on any real device, which fingerprint consistency detectors (Pixelscan, Fingerprint.com) can identify as "masking."

**Specifically:** The WebGL vendor/renderer is sampled from `webgl.py` independently of the BrowserForge screen resolution and navigator platform. The font subset is generated from the OS font list independently of the GPU profile. A real device with a specific GPU (e.g., Intel Iris Xe) ships with specific screen resolutions and a specific font set — the synthetic generation doesn't enforce this correlation.

**Evidence from testing:** Running Camoufox v152.0.4-beta.28 (headed via Xvfb, no proxy, residential IP) against the Pixelscan fingerprint check:

- Browser: Firefox 152.0 on Ubuntu — ✅ (correctly spoofed)
- Location: Australia / Mango Hill — ✅ (GeoIP matched)
- Proxy: No proxy detected — ✅
- Bot check: No automated behavior detected — ✅
- **Fingerprint: Masking detected** — ❌ ("Your Browser Fingerprint is inconsistent")

The browser integrity, location, proxy, and bot detection checks all pass. Only fingerprint consistency fails — indicating the spoofed properties don't form a coherent device profile.

**Note:** This affects the BrowserForge synthetic path. The bundled `fingerprint-presets.json` and `fingerprint-presets-v150.json` presets (from real devices) should be internally consistent already.

### Screenshots:

Pixelscan results showing "Masking detected" with all other checks passing:

![pixelscan-fingerprint-masking](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/pixelscan-fingerprint-masking.png)

### To Reproduce:

1. Launch Camoufox v152.0.4-beta.28 with default BrowserForge fingerprint generation (no preset)
2. Navigate to `https://pixelscan.net/fingerprint-check`
3. Observe "Masking detected" on the Fingerprint card while Browser, Location, Proxy, and Bot check all pass

```python
from camoufox.sync_api import Camoufox

with Camoufox(headless="virtual") as browser:
    page = browser.new_page()
    page.goto("https://pixelscan.net/fingerprint-check")
    page.wait_for_timeout(30000)
    page.screenshot(path="pixelscan.png")
```

### Version:

```
Browser: v152.0.4-beta.28
BrowserForge: v1.2.4
OS: Linux x86_64 (headed via Xvfb :99, 1920x1080x24)
```

### Proposed solution

Add a consistency validation step in `generate_context_fingerprint()` (Python layer, `pythonlib/camoufox/fingerprints.py`) that ensures cross-property coherence when using BrowserForge synthetic generation:

1. **WebGL ↔ screen resolution:** When sampling WebGL vendor/renderer from `webgl.py`, restrict to GPU profiles that are commonly paired with the BrowserForge screen resolution (e.g., a 1366x768 screen shouldn't claim a high-end discrete GPU)
2. **WebGL ↔ OS platform:** Already partially handled (OS map in the WebGL sampling), but could be tighter
3. **Fonts ↔ OS:** Already handled via `_generate_random_font_subset(os_name)`, but marker font injection should match the claimed platform
4. **Voices ↔ OS:** Already handled via `_generate_random_voice_subset(os_name)`

The main gap is #1 — the WebGL profile and screen resolution are independently sampled and can form combinations that don't exist on real hardware. A lookup table mapping GPU profiles to common screen resolutions would close this.

This is a Python-only change in `fingerprints.py` — no C++/browser patch needed.

title: Juggler Protocol Rejects isMobile context prop from Playwright v1.62.1 in Browser.setDefaultViewport
body:
### Describe the bug:

Newer Playwright versions send an `isMobile` property as part of the `Browser.setDefaultViewport` request https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/41179. Camoufox's Juggler protocol currently rejects this property because it is not defined in the protocol schema.

Error:

```text
browser.newContext: Protocol error (Browser.setDefaultViewport):
Found property "<root>.viewport.isMobile" - false which is not described in this scheme
```

The validation appears to originate from https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/blob/main/additions/juggler/protocol/PrimitiveTypes.js#L99, where unknown properties are rejected.

Playwright is sending:

```json
{
  "viewportSize": {
    "width": 1280,
    "height": 720
  },
  "deviceScaleFactor": 1,
  "isMobile": false
}
```

This can happen even when `isMobile` is not explicitly specified by the user.

It appears that the Camoufox Juggler schema needs to be updated to recognize `isMobile`, or otherwise ignore it if Camoufox does not use the property.

### Screenshots:

Not applicable. The protocol error is included above.

### To Reproduce:

```javascript
newContext({
  viewport: {
    width: 1280,
    height: 720
  }
});
```

With the affected Playwright/Camoufox versions, this results in the `Browser.setDefaultViewport` protocol error above.

### Version:

```text
$ python -m camoufox version
v152.0.4-beta.28
```

Playwright:

```text
$ npx playwright --version
v1.62.1
```

title: License clarification for the Python package (camoufox 0.5.4)
body:
Hi, thank you for maintaining Camoufox.

I'm maintaining a private/local tool that uses `camoufox==0.5.4`. While doing a third-party license audit for a possible bundled Windows build, I noticed a licensing ambiguity around the Python package and wanted to ask for clarification before making any redistribution assumptions.

What I found from the official artifacts:

- PyPI metadata for `camoufox 0.5.4` declares MIT (`License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License`).
- The installed `camoufox-0.5.4.dist-info/METADATA` also declares MIT.
- `pythonlib/pyproject.toml` at the corresponding source revision declares MIT.
- However, I could not find an MIT license file / copyright notice in the 0.5.4 wheel, sdist, or `pythonlib/` directory.
- The repository root `LICENSE` is MPL-2.0, so I don't want to assume that it should be substituted for the separately-declared MIT license of the Python wrapper.

Could you clarify which exact license text and copyright notice redistributors of the Python package should retain?

If the Python wrapper is intended to be MIT-licensed, adding a `LICENSE` file under `pythonlib/` (or otherwise identifying the authoritative MIT notice) would make the intended terms unambiguous for downstream packaging.

If the package metadata is outdated and the Python wrapper is actually intended to follow another license, clarification of that would also be very helpful.

No public redistribution is currently being made on my side; I'm asking so the dependency can be documented correctly and so any future packaging can preserve the intended upstream notice.

Thanks.

title: fix: verify SHA256 digest after download and enable TLS verification for IP lookup
body:
## Related Issue

Closes #715

## Description

Two security fixes in the Python package:

### 1. SHA256 digest verification after download

In `multiversion.py:install_versioned()`, the release asset's SHA256 digest is fetched from the GitHub API and stored in `installed_sha256`, but it is never compared to the downloaded bytes. The digest is only written to `version.json` as metadata after extraction.

This adds a verification step between download and extraction: compute `hashlib.sha256` of the downloaded archive and compare to `expected_sha256`. On mismatch, the install directory is cleaned up and an exception is raised.

### 2. TLS verification for public IP lookup

In `ip.py:public_ip()`, all HTTP requests to IP lookup APIs disable TLS verification (`verify=False`) and suppress the `InsecureRequestWarning`. This means the IP lookup is vulnerable to MITM — an attacker could inject a fake IP response, which would then be used for geolocation/timezone spoofing.

This removes `verify=False` and the `_suppress_insecure_warning()` context manager. All requests now use default TLS verification. The IP lookup APIs (`api.ipify.org`, `checkip.amazonaws.com`, etc.) all support HTTPS with valid certificates.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Testing

- `camoufox fetch` still works — downloads and extracts successfully
- SHA256 verification passes on valid download (verified digest matches)
- SHA256 verification raises on corrupted download (tested with truncated file)
- `public_ip()` still resolves correctly over TLS (tested from Linux server)
- No `InsecureRequestWarning` warnings in output

## Checklist

- [x] I have linked a related issue above
- [x] My changes are focused on a single logical change
- [x] I have added testing instructions which include the desired result

title: fix: Docker build improvements — disable debug symbols, add ccache, add .dockerignore
body:
## Related Issue

Closes #698

## Description

Three Docker build fixes:

1. **Add `--disable-debug-symbols` to `assets/linux.mozconfig`** — Distribution builds don't ship symbols anyway. Debug info inflates memory usage at the link stage, causing OOM kills on arm64 builds (the `gkrust` fat-LTO staticlib + `libxul` link peaks past available RAM). This keeps the link under the RAM ceiling and shrinks the binary.

2. **Add `ccache` to Dockerfile apt-get install** — `assets/base.mozconfig` already has a conditional `if command -v ccache` check, but the Dockerfile never installs ccache, so every Docker build runs cold. Adding ccache to the package list makes the conditional actually trigger, enabling incremental build caching.

3. **Add `.dockerignore`** — Without it, `COPY . /app` ships `.git`, `dist/`, `node_modules/`, and built artifacts into the build context. This trims the context substantially and prevents `patch.py`'s `git clean -fdx` from walking up to the host git work tree created by `COPY . /app`.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Testing

- arm64 build completes without OOM (previously SIGKILLed at link stage)
- Subsequent Docker builds use ccache (cold build ~40min, warm ~5min)
- Build context reduced from >500MB to <50MB

## Checklist

- [x] I have linked a related issue above
- [x] My changes are focused on a single logical change
- [x] I have added testing instructions which include the desired result

title: fix(addons): re-download addons with a missing manifest (#308)
body:
## Related Issue

Closes #308

## Description

`maybe_download_addons()` treated an addon as already downloaded whenever its directory existed (`os.path.exists(addon_path)`). A download that fails partway leaves an empty directory behind, and that empty dir is then trusted on every later launch. `confirm_paths()` still requires `manifest.json`, so the launch fails with `InvalidAddonPath: manifest.json is missing` and never recovers without manually deleting the cache.

Fix:
- Gate the "already downloaded" check on `manifest.json` being present, not on the bare directory.
- `shutil.rmtree` the partial directory when a download fails, so the next run re-downloads instead of caching a broken state.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Testing

Added `pythonlib/tests/test_addons.py` (no network; `download_and_extract` is monkeypatched):
- an empty addon dir triggers a re-download
- a dir with `manifest.json` is not re-downloaded
- a failed download removes the partial dir

`cd pythonlib && python -m pytest tests/test_addons.py -v` -> 3 passed. Both bug-guarding tests fail on current main and pass with this change.

## Fingerprint Report

This changes addon download/caching only, with no fingerprint or browser-patch surface, so neither tester applies. service-tester is out of service upstream; build-tester covers browser-patch changes. Verified with the unit tests above.

title: canvas:seed is declared and passed through, but nothing consumes it
body:
## Who's asking I maintain [camoufox-profile-manager](https://github.com/polyackiy/camoufox-profile-manager), an open-source, self-hosted profile manager built on Camoufox — roughly what AdsPower or Dolphin do commercially, for people who would rather run it themselves. Camoufox does the hard part; we manage profiles, proxies, groups and the browser lifecycle around it. Thanks for the browser. Pinning a resolved config and replaying it across launches works beautifully — user agent, screen, GPU, cores, audio and fonts all hold steady, which is exactly what a long-lived profile needs. **This is not a request to change any default.** We have a working setup and are not blocked. It is a report that one advertised property appears to be inert, in case that is news to you. ### Describe the bug: #### The finding `canvas:seed` is advertised as a config property but nothing seems to consume it: - Declared in `settings/properties.json` and `settings/camoucfg.jvv` - Generated and passed by `pythonlib/camoufox/utils.py` (`set_into(config, 'canvas:seed', randint(...))`) - Referenced by `tests/patches/config-overrides.py` - **Not read anywhere in `additions/camoucfg/MaskConfig.hpp`**, and no patch in `patches/` mentions canvas `audio:seed` and `fonts:spacing_seed` sit beside it in the same code paths and do take effect, which is what made this surprising. Setting `canvas:seed` to any value produces no change in the exported canvas. Relatedly, `docs/per-context-patches.md` documents `window.setCanvasSeed()`, but it is `undefined` in the shipped build while its siblings are defined: ``` window.setCanvasSeed undefined window.setNavigatorUserAgent function window.setWebGLVendor function ``` If that work simply is not released yet, this may already be handled on your side — a pointer is all we need. ### To Reproduce: Camoufox `152.0.4-beta.28`, Python lib 0.5.x, macOS arm64.
canvas_seed_repro.py ```python """Reproduction: canvas:seed does not affect the 2D canvas fingerprint. Camoufox 152.0.4-beta.28, Python lib 0.5.x. pip install camoufox[geoip] && camoufox fetch python canvas_seed_repro.py Every check below is printed with what was expected, so the output stands on its own. """ import asyncio import hashlib import tempfile from pathlib import Path from camoufox.async_api import AsyncCamoufox # A page reads its canvas the way a fingerprinting script would. CANVAS = """() => { const c = document.createElement('canvas'); c.width = 300; c.height = 70; const x = c.getContext('2d'); x.textBaseline = 'top'; x.font = '16px Arial'; x.fillStyle = '#f60'; x.fillRect(0, 0, 120, 25); x.fillStyle = '#069'; x.fillText('canvas probe', 2, 18); return c.toDataURL(); }""" SITE = "https://example.com" OTHER_SITE = "https://iana.org" def digest(value: str) -> str: return hashlib.sha256(value.encode()).hexdigest()[:16] async def read_canvas(context, url=SITE): page = await context.new_page() await page.goto(url, wait_until="domcontentloaded", timeout=45000) value = digest(await page.evaluate(CANVAS)) await page.close() return value async def main(): root = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="canvas-seed-")) seed_config = {"canvas:seed": 424242} def options(profile_dir): return dict( headless=True, os="windows", i_know_what_im_doing=True, persistent_context=True, user_data_dir=str(root / profile_dir), config=dict(seed_config), ) print("Camoufox canvas:seed reproduction") print("=" * 66) # 1. Within one session the value is stable per site. This is correct. async with AsyncCamoufox(**options("a")) as context: first_tab = await read_canvas(context) second_tab = await read_canvas(context) other_site = await read_canvas(context, OTHER_SITE) print("\nWithin one session, canvas:seed = 424242") print(f" same site, tab 1 {first_tab}") print(f" same site, tab 2 {second_tab} equal: {first_tab == second_tab} (expected: equal)") print(f" a different site {other_site} equal: {first_tab == other_site} (expected: not equal)") # 2. Across launches of the SAME profile with the SAME seed, it changes. # This is the bug: the seed should make it reproducible. async with AsyncCamoufox(**options("a")) as context: second_launch = await read_canvas(context) async with AsyncCamoufox(**options("a")) as context: third_launch = await read_canvas(context) print("\nSame profile, same seed, relaunched") print(f" launch 1 {first_tab}") print(f" launch 2 {second_launch}") print(f" launch 3 {third_launch}") stable = first_tab == second_launch == third_launch print(f" all equal: {stable} (expected: equal, since the seed is fixed)") # 3. Two different seeds, fresh profiles: no relationship either way. async with AsyncCamoufox(**{**options("b"), "config": {"canvas:seed": 111}}) as context: seed_111 = await read_canvas(context) async with AsyncCamoufox(**{**options("c"), "config": {"canvas:seed": 999}}) as context: seed_999 = await read_canvas(context) print("\nDifferent seeds, fresh profiles") print(f" canvas:seed = 111 {seed_111}") print(f" canvas:seed = 999 {seed_999}") # 4. Is the per-context API from docs/per-context-patches.md present? async with AsyncCamoufox(headless=True, os="windows", i_know_what_im_doing=True) as browser: page = await browser.new_page() await page.goto("about:blank") present = await page.evaluate( """() => ({ setCanvasSeed: typeof window.setCanvasSeed, setNavigatorUserAgent: typeof window.setNavigatorUserAgent, setWebGLVendor: typeof window.setWebGLVendor, })""" ) print("\nPer-context API in this build") for name, kind in present.items(): print(f" window.{name:24} {kind}") print("\n" + "=" * 66) print("Result:", "seed is honoured" if stable else "the seed has no effect on the canvas fingerprint") asyncio.run(main()) ```
``` Within one session, canvas:seed = 424242 same site, tab 1 cc9159d5dd44dc0e same site, tab 2 cc9159d5dd44dc0e equal: True (expected: equal) a different site 425ea3469ee3f27c equal: False (expected: not equal) Same profile, same seed, relaunched launch 1 cc9159d5dd44dc0e launch 2 57f921e26a94bcdc launch 3 abcf3e69880a54fe all equal: False (expected: equal, since the seed is fixed) Per-context API in this build window.setCanvasSeed undefined ``` The first block is correct behaviour: stable per site within a session, different across sites. Only the seed is the issue. ## Scope, for the record Since I had to measure this precisely, in case it saves you time: | Surface | Behaviour | | --- | --- | | `toDataURL()` / `toBlob()`, **2D** context | randomised per site, per session | | `toDataURL()`, **WebGL** context | randomised the same way | | `getImageData()` | stable | | `readPixels()` | stable | | `measureText()` | stable | So it is image export that is randomised, from either context type. ## What we do instead For completeness, so this does not read as a blocker: launching with `privacy.baselineFingerprintingProtection = false` disables the randomisation, and combined with a pinned `fonts:spacing_seed` the canvas becomes reproducible across launches. Text-bearing canvases need that second part — that is what misled me at first, since the font seed masked the pref's effect. That workaround costs cross-site unlinkability: the canvas becomes identical everywhere. For one long-lived account per profile that is the right trade and matches what a real machine does, so we will expose it as a per-profile setting rather than a default. A working `canvas:seed` would be strictly better than the pref, because it would give each profile its own canvas value instead of one shared true render — which is why the report is still worth making. ## Offer Happy to write the patch if you can point at where the export randomisation is applied; I could not find it from the repository alone and would rather not guess at C++ I cannot build and test here. I can also verify any build against the reproduction above on macOS arm64 and Linux x86_64 and report back. If the intended behaviour is that `canvas:seed` is reserved for the unreleased per-context work, feel free to close this — it would be worth a note in the property manifest either way, since the Python layer emits it today. ### Version: ``` Python Packages Camoufox v0.5.4 Browserforge v1.2.4 Apify Fingerprints v0.15.0 Playwright v1.60.0 Browser Active official/stable Current browser v152.0.4-beta.28 ``` Host: macOS 15 arm64. Also reproduced on Linux x86_64.

title: Runtime.evaluate with infinite loop (while(true){}) poisons entire browser context — no protocol-level interrupt
body:
## Describe the bug

When `Runtime.evaluate` is called with JavaScript that runs an infinite loop (e.g. `while(true){}`), the evaluate call hangs as expected. However, after the evaluate times out on the client side, the **entire browser context becomes permanently unresponsive**. All subsequent `Runtime.evaluate` calls on any page in the same context hang indefinitely.

The JS event loop for the entire context is blocked by the infinite loop. There is no way to interrupt it at the protocol level — the only recovery is closing and recreating the browser context (or killing the browser process).

## Environment

- Camoufox: v152.0.4-beta.28
- OS: Debian bookworm (Docker container)
- Launcher: direct Juggler pipe (Rust server)

## To Reproduce

1. Create a browser context and a page
2. Send `Runtime.evaluate` with expression `while(true){}`
3. Wait for the client-side timeout (e.g. 30s)
4. Try any `Runtime.evaluate` on the same page — hangs indefinitely
5. Try any `Runtime.evaluate` on a *different* page in the *same* context — also hangs
6. `Page.navigate` on any page in the context — hangs
7. Only `Browser.createBrowserContext` + `Browser.newPage` on a *new* context works

## Expected behavior

The Juggler protocol should support terminating a stuck `Runtime.evaluate`:
- A `Runtime.terminateEvaluate` or `Runtime.interrupt` command that forcefully stops the JS execution
- Or: the evaluate timeout should be enforced at the protocol level (not just the client side), with the JS engine interrupted when the deadline passes
- Or: the evaluate should run in a worker that can be terminated without affecting the main context's event loop

Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) has `Runtime.runIfWaitingForDebugger` and supports terminating evaluations. Juggler currently has no equivalent.

## Actual behavior

The JS event loop is shared across all pages in the context. A single `while(true){}` blocks everything. The protocol provides no way to interrupt it. The only recovery is destroying the context.

## Impact

We've implemented a workaround in our server: when an evaluate times out, a background task closes and recreates the poisoned context (`Browser.removeBrowserContext` + `Browser.createBrowserContext`). This works but is destructive — all tabs and session state in that context are lost. A protocol-level interrupt would be non-destructive and much cleaner.

## Suggestion

Could the Juggler protocol add:
1. A `Runtime.terminateEvaluate` method that sends a JS interrupt signal
2. Or enforce evaluate timeouts at the protocol level (the server kills the evaluate when the deadline passes, rather than the client timing out)
3. Or document whether `Page.close` on a stuck page releases the JS event loop (it doesn't appear to)

This is especially important for automation servers that evaluate untrusted/uncontrolled JS from web pages — a single page with an infinite loop shouldn't require destroying the entire context.

title: Juggler pipe becomes unresponsive while browser process stays alive (dead pipe state)
body:
## Describe the bug

When the browser navigates to certain pages (e.g. Cloudflare-protected sites, heavy SPAs), the Juggler pipe stops responding to commands — `Browser.newPage`, `Page.navigate`, and `Runtime.evaluate` all hang indefinitely. The browser **process stays alive** (`/proc/PID` exists, `browser_alive: true`) but no Juggler command completes.

The process does not crash — there is no exit signal, no error on stderr, no `Browser.disconnected` event. The pipe is simply silent. This is a **dead pipe** state: the process is alive but the Juggler protocol handler is unresponsive.

## Environment

- Camoufox: v152.0.4-beta.28
- OS: Debian bookworm (Docker container)
- Launcher: direct Juggler pipe (not via Playwright/camoufox-js Python wrapper)
- Our server: a Rust HTTP server that drives Camoufox via Juggler pipes (fd 3/4)

## To Reproduce

1. Launch Camoufox with `-juggler-pipe` flag
2. Send `Browser.enable` — works, Juggler initializes
3. Create contexts via `Browser.createBrowserContext` — works
4. Create pages via `Browser.newPage` — works for normal sites
5. Navigate to a Cloudflare-protected page (e.g. `https://simplywall.st/dashboard`)
6. After some navigations, `Browser.newPage` starts hanging — no response, no error
7. `Browser.enable` was already called, the process is alive, but no Juggler command completes
8. The only recovery is killing and relaunching the process

## Expected behavior

The Juggler protocol should either:
- Continue responding to `Browser.newPage` and other commands even when a page's JS is heavy (the protocol handler runs on a separate thread from the page's JS engine)
- Emit a `Browser.disconnected` or error event when the pipe becomes unresponsive
- Provide a protocol-level heartbeat/ping that can detect a dead pipe

## Actual behavior

The process stays alive indefinitely. The Juggler pipe handler stops responding to all commands. No error is emitted. There is no way to detect the dead pipe from the protocol level — the only signal is a timeout on `send`.

## Impact

We've implemented a workaround in our server: a `dead_pipe` flag set when `Session::send` times out, with a crash-recovery monitor that restarts the browser. This works but is a server-side detection of a problem that ideally shouldn't happen — the Juggler protocol handler should remain responsive even when a page's main thread is blocked.

## Related issues

- #553 — parallelization hang in `new_page()` (may be related — concurrent newPage calls blocking)
- #620 — Juggler XPCOM never initializes (different root cause but same symptom: process alive, Juggler unresponsive)
- #572 — Juggler browser hangs (read-only environment, different root cause)

## Suggestion

Could the Juggler protocol handler run on a separate thread from the page's JS event loop? Or could a protocol-level ping (`Browser.ping` or similar) be added that always responds regardless of page state? This would let automation servers detect a dead pipe without relying on send timeouts.

title: [Feature] Config lever for PublicKeyCredential.isUserVerifyingPlatformAuthenticatorAvailable() (uvpaa) — always false, incoherent for macOS / Windows-Hello profiles
body:
### Summary
`PublicKeyCredential.isUserVerifyingPlatformAuthenticatorAvailable()` (uvpaa) always
resolves to `false` regardless of the spoofed OS. For fingerprint profiles that emulate
devices which overwhelmingly ship a platform authenticator — MacBooks with Touch ID, or
Windows PCs with Windows Hello — a real Firefox returns `true`. Camoufox returning `false`
is a coherence signal (reads as headless/VM/no-biometric). Requesting a config lever to
control it.

### Environment
- Camoufox 152.0.4-beta.28, **headless**, driven via Playwright (sync API), Windows host.
- Tested on an HTTPS origin (secure context required for `PublicKeyCredential`).

### Reproduction (HTTPS page)
```js
await PublicKeyCredential.isUserVerifyingPlatformAuthenticatorAvailable() // → false
await PublicKeyCredential.isConditionalMediationAvailable()               // → true
navigator.platform                                                        // "MacIntel" (os="macos")  |  "Win32" (os="windows")

title: [Bug] speechSynthesis leaks host Windows SAPI voices on non-Windows (os=linux/macos) profiles; no default voice
body:
### Summary
On a headless launch with `os="linux"` or `os="macos"`, `speechSynthesis.getVoices()`
returns the **host machine's Windows SAPI voices** (`urn:moz-tts:sapi:` URIs) instead of a
spoofed, OS-appropriate list:
- Real **Linux** Firefox emits `urn:moz-tts:speechd:` (espeak) voices.
- Real **macOS** Firefox emits `urn:moz-tts:osx:` voices.
- Windows `sapi:` voices on a claimed Linux/macOS profile is a hard OS lie, and it leaks the
  host OS (Windows) plus its installed language packs.

Two additional problems on **all** OS profiles:
1. `getVoices()` contains **0 voices with `default === true`** (real Firefox always has exactly one).
2. On `os="windows"` the list is the host's *real* installed voices, so it still leaks the
   host's specific language packs rather than a coherent spoofed set.

Camoufox's generated config ships a per-OS voices array, but it does not appear to be
registered by `MaskConfig::MVoices` in this build — the native SAPI backend is enumerated instead.

### Environment
- Camoufox **152.0.4-beta.28**, headless, **Windows** host, Playwright sync API.
- Minimal config: only `os=` set. No proxy/geoip. Tested on an HTTPS origin.

### Reproduction
```python
from camoufox.sync_api import Camoufox
for osc in ["linux", "macos", "windows"]:
    with Camoufox(headless=True, os=osc) as b:
        p = b.new_page(); p.goto("https://example.com/"); p.wait_for_timeout(1500)
        uris = p.evaluate("() => speechSynthesis.getVoices().map(v => v.voiceURI)")
        defs = p.evaluate("() => speechSynthesis.getVoices().filter(v => v.default).length")
        print(osc, "defaults=", defs, uris[:4])
```

**Actual** — identical for `linux`, `macos`, and `windows`, `defaults=0`:
```
urn:moz-tts:sapi:Microsoft David - English (United States)?en-US
urn:moz-tts:sapi:Microsoft Zira - English (United States)?en-US
urn:moz-tts:sapi:Microsoft Mark - English (United States)?en-US
...(the host's other installed SAPI language-pack voices)
```
i.e. Windows `sapi:` voices are returned even when `navigator.platform` is `Linux x86_64` / `MacIntel`.

### Expected
- `os=linux` → `urn:moz-tts:speechd:` voices (or the config-provided list).
- `os=macos` → `urn:moz-tts:osx:` voices.
- `os=windows` → `sapi:` voices from a spoofed/coherent set, not the host's real installed packs.
- Exactly one voice with `default === true`.

### Attempted mitigations
- `voices:blockIfNotDefined = true` → `getVoices()` returns `[]` (stops the leak, but an empty
  list is itself slightly abnormal). Current workaround.
- `media.webspeech.synth.enabled = false` → removes `speechSynthesis` entirely (bigger tell).

### Impact
High for stealth: a spoofed macOS/Linux profile exposing Windows `sapi:` voices (and the host's
language packs) is trivially cross-checked (voice backend vs `navigator.platform`) by
CreepJS-class fingerprinters.

title: Verify downloaded release assets and stop disabling TLS verification
body:
## Related Issue

Closes #715

## Description

Two fixes in `pythonlib/`, one commit each.

**`Verify sha256 of downloaded release assets before extracting`**

`check_asset()` already parses the asset's `digest` from the GitHub API into `installed_sha256`, and `AvailableVersion.sha256` carries it into `version.json` — but nothing ever compared it against the downloaded bytes, so the archive that gets extracted over the install dir and `chmod 755`'d was accepted on transport security alone.

Adds `verify_sha256()` in `pkgman.py` and calls it between download and extraction on **both** install paths: `install_versioned()` (CLI) and `InstallWorker.run()` (GUI). Hashes in 1 MiB blocks so a multi-hundred-megabyte asset is not held in memory, and rewinds the buffer so `unzip()` still reads from position 0.

When no digest is published it warns and proceeds rather than failing — refusing to install from a source that publishes no digest would be a regression, not a fix.

**`Enable TLS verification for public IP lookups`**

`public_ip()` used `verify=False` inside a context manager that also silenced urllib3's `InsecureRequestWarning`. Since these requests are routed through the user's proxy, a forged response controls the value used to spoof the WebRTC IP.

Sets `verify=True` and removes the suppression helper. `requests` raises `SSLError`, a subclass of `RequestException` that the existing loop already catches, so a host with a bad certificate is now skipped in favour of the next entry in `URLS` instead of being trusted.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Other

## Testing

New: `pythonlib/tests/test_download_integrity.py` — 12 tests.

```bash
cd pythonlib && python -m pytest tests/ -q
```

**Result: 57 passed, 2 failed.** The 2 failures are `test_virtdisplay.py::test_single_launch_...` and `::test_concurrent_reservations_...`, which fail identically on unmodified `main` in this environment — not introduced here.

What the new tests pin:

| Case | Expected |
|---|---|
| Digest matches | accepted |
| Digest differs in case | accepted |
| First byte flipped | `CorruptedDownload` |
| Last bit flipped | `CorruptedDownload` |
| Truncated by one byte | `CorruptedDownload` |
| One byte appended | `CorruptedDownload` |
| Empty payload | `CorruptedDownload` |
| Error message | names the asset and both digests |
| Digest `None` / `""` | proceeds with a warning |
| Buffer after verify | rewound to 0, fully readable |
| Real `NamedTemporaryFile` | verified and rewound |

The payload spans several read blocks, so a single-shot `read()` regression cannot pass by accident.

TLS change verified live — `public_ip()` returns normally with `verify=True`, and no `verify=False` or `InsecureRequestWarning` reference remains in the package.

## Fingerprint Report

**Not applicable — no browser patches or C++/JS browser-layer code touched.** This PR changes only `pythonlib/` (download integrity + an HTTP client flag); no fingerprint surface is affected.

Per the checklist below, build-tester covers patch changes, and service-tester — the suite that would apply to `pythonlib/` changes — is currently marked out of service. It also requires real proxies, which I do not have. Happy to run either if you'd like.

N/A — see above.

title: Release assets are extracted without checking their sha256, and public IP lookups run with TLS verification disabled
body:
Two issues in `pythonlib/`, both in code paths that exist to protect the user. Reporting together because they are one-line-ish fixes in the same package; happy to split into separate issues if you'd prefer.

### 1. Downloaded release assets are never verified against their digest

`webdl()` streams a release asset into a buffer, `install_versioned()` hands that buffer straight to `unzip()`, and the extracted tree is then `chmod -R 755`'d and executed.

The digest is already available. `PkgManager.check_asset()` reads it from the GitHub API response and stores it:

```python
digest = asset.get('digest') or ''
if digest.startswith('sha256:'):
    self.installed_sha256 = digest.split(':', 1)[1]
```

`AvailableVersion.sha256` carries it further, into `version.json`. But it is never compared against the downloaded bytes. Every `sha256 ==` comparison in the package compares metadata to metadata to identify *which installed version* a folder holds; `hashlib` appears once, in `utils.py`, to key a config cache.

So the archive is accepted on transport security alone. A truncated download, a bad mirror, or a substituted asset all extract silently.

**Repro:** point `webdl()` at a modified archive — installation completes normally, `version.json` records the *expected* sha256 that the installed bytes do not have.

### 2. `public_ip()` disables TLS certificate verification

`camoufox/ip.py`:

```python
with _suppress_insecure_warning():
    resp = requests.get(url, ..., verify=False)
```

`_suppress_insecure_warning()` filters out urllib3's `InsecureRequestWarning`, so the disabled verification is also silent.

These requests go **through the user's proxy** when one is configured — the exact position an attacker occupies. A forged response controls what `public_ip()` returns, and callers use that to spoof the WebRTC IP. `validate_ip()` constrains the result to a well-formed address, but which address is the attacker's choice, so the leak the function exists to prevent becomes attacker-selectable.

The `ip-api.com` lookups in `sync_api.py` / `async_api.py` have a related weakness (plain `http://`), but that appears to be forced by ip-api's free tier, so I have left it alone rather than break the feature.

### Environment

Reproduced on `main` @ f1febf4, Python 3.13, Linux.

### Fix

PR follows — `verify=True` plus a `verify_sha256()` call between download and extraction on both install paths, with 12 unit tests. No browser patches touched.
