title: Replace vendored test suite with version-resolved upstream pull
body:
## Summary

The `tests/` directory is a 2-year-stale vendored copy of `microsoft/playwright-python/tests/`. Symptoms include:

- Imports of APIs that no longer exist (`Page.accessibility`, `playwright._impl._glob.glob_to_regex`).
- 9 critical-primitive tests renamed `.disabled` instead of fixed (`test_click`, `test_fill`, `test_focus`, `test_check`, `test_dispatch_event`, `test_element_handle`, `test_launcher`, `test_popup`, `test_browsercontext_client_certificates`).
- `tests/conftest.py:83` passing `os.getenv("HEADLESS")` straight to Playwright, which now rejects strings — meaning nobody had run the suite with `HEADLESS=1` after that line landed.
- Test server returning empty-bodied 404 / 401 responses, hanging Firefox's `wait_until=load`.
- 19+ test files that exist upstream simply absent from the vendored copy.

The result: a ~95-failure suite that gates nothing because nobody runs it. None of the open PRs against this repo can rely on it.

## What this PR does

Replaces the entire vendored `tests/` directory with `tests-camoufox/` — a small, self-contained harness that **pulls upstream tests from `microsoft/playwright-python` at the tag matching the installed `playwright` package version, on demand**.

```
tests-camoufox/
├── README.md                    architecture + bump instructions
├── local-requirements.txt       single source of truth: playwright==1.59.0
├── setup-venv.sh                pulls upstream@v<X.Y.Z>'s test deps too
├── run-tests.sh                 entry point: clone-on-demand + pytest
├── camoufox_plugin.py           loaded into upstream pytest run
├── conftest.py                  Camoufox-only test fixtures
├── known-failures-v1.59.0.txt   real Camoufox bugs, categorised + commented
├── pyproject.toml
├── test_stealth_smoke.py        wraps build-tester as a pytest case
├── test_launch_arg_vs_spoof.py  pins UA / locale / timezone / webdriver
├── test_virtual_display.py      Xvfb integration (skips if Xvfb absent)
└── .upstream-cache/             gitignored; v1.59.0/, v1.60.0/, ...
```

**Version resolution**:

```
local-requirements.txt:playwright==1.59.0
        │
        └── installed package version
                │
                └── pulls microsoft/playwright-python@v1.59.0 tarball
                          │
                          └── pytest tests/async/ -p camoufox_plugin
                                    + the 3 Camoufox-only test_*.py files
```

To bump:

```bash
# Edit local-requirements.txt: playwright==1.60.0
rm -rf venv .upstream-cache
bash tests-camoufox/setup-venv.sh
./tests-camoufox/run-tests.sh --executable-path /path/to/camoufox
```

The pytest plugin (`camoufox_plugin.py`) monkey-patches `BrowserType.launch` and `launch_persistent_context` to inject `CAMOUFOX_EXECUTABLE_PATH`, regardless of which conftest fixture the test happens to use. It also skips headed-only tests cleanly when `DISPLAY` is unset.

## Camoufox-specific tests

Three test files cover what upstream can't:

- **`test_stealth_smoke.py`** — runs the existing `build-tester/` suite as a single pytest case, fails on a >1% drop in pass-ratio. The current 953/956 baseline passes.
- **`test_launch_arg_vs_spoof.py`** — pins UA, locale, timezone, and `navigator.webdriver` behaviour at the launch-arg-vs-fingerprint boundary. The known locale-spoof-wins bug is `xfail`-marked; it'll start passing automatically when fixed.
- **`test_virtual_display.py`** — spawns Xvfb directly, launches Camoufox headed against it, asserts no headless-mode UA / `navigator.webdriver` leakage. Skips cleanly when Xvfb isn't installed.

## Baseline against v146.0.1-beta.25.2

```
upstream Playwright suite:  1366 passed, 56 skipped, 0 failed (after known-failures deselects)
camoufox-specific:          7 passed, 1 xfailed (the known locale bug)
total runtime:              ~13 minutes on -n 8
```

`known-failures-v1.59.0.txt` documents the 30+ real Camoufox bugs the upstream suite exposes, categorised:

- 10 proxy-related (`firefox.launch(proxy=...)` ignored)
- 8 navigation history (go_back, reload(data:), dom_history, har redirects)
- 5 client-certificate tests (Camoufox patches alter cert handling)
- 2 locale-launch-arg-vs-fingerprint
- 2 expose_function + add_init_script
- 1 keyboard double-input event
- 1 video record_video_dir auto-finalize
- whole `test_page_clock.py` and `test_tracing.py` modules (clock-spoof variance, trace event ordering)
- a handful of one-off divergences and one harness hang

The format encourages **shrinking** the list — each follow-up fix branch removes lines from this file rather than amending them. Once a real bug is fixed, its line goes away and the test counts toward the green baseline.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (test infrastructure)
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation update
- [x] Other — replaces existing test infrastructure

## Testing

```bash
bash tests-camoufox/setup-venv.sh
./tests-camoufox/run-tests.sh --executable-path /path/to/camoufox
```

Runs upstream's full Playwright async suite plus our 8 Camoufox-specific tests against any Camoufox binary. Output should be `OK` on a clean Camoufox build.

## Why version-resolved-clone instead of vendoring

The vendored copy went stale because nothing forces it to track upstream — it diverges silently. Pulling at a pinned tag forces every Playwright bump to be a deliberate decision (change the pin, rerun, triage new failures) and gets every upstream test improvement for free (`test_check`, `test_screencast`, `test_extension`, `test_route_web_socket` all appear automatically once we point at v1.59.0 instead of the older snapshot the vendored copy was based on).

This is similar to how [Patchright](https://github.com/Kaliiiiiiiiii-Vinyzu/patchright) handles its test suite — they run upstream Playwright's tests on every release, which is the main reason that fork stays stable.

## Checklist

- [x] No browser code changes — `additions/`, `patches/`, `pythonlib/` untouched.
- [x] Removes 210 files (the entire `tests/` directory).
- [x] Adds 12 files under `tests-camoufox/`.
- [x] CI hookable: a single shell command runs the whole suite.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: feat: add persistent fingerprint seeds
body:
## Summary

  Adds an optional `fingerprint_seed` parameter for Camoufox-generated
  fingerprints so callers can reproduce stable generated identity values across
  launches and browser contexts.

  Related issues/discussions:

  - Addresses #442
  - Addresses #38
  - Addresses #71
  - Addresses #328
  - Addresses #378
  - Related to discussions #263, #373, #151, and #255

  This is intentionally Python/API-level only. It does not include browser engine,
  C++, TLS, networking, or renderer-level fingerprinting changes.

  ## Motivation

  Camoufox is good at generating fresh fingerprints, but persistent profiles need
  a way to keep generated fingerprint values stable across restarts. Several users
  have reported that cookies/storage can persist while generated fingerprint
  surfaces still rotate, causing CreepJS/fingerprint IDs or browser identity
  signals to change between runs.

  `fingerprint_seed` gives callers a stable generation input while preserving the
  current random-by-default behavior when no seed is supplied.

  ## What Changed

  - Added deterministic seed derivation helpers in `pythonlib/camoufox/` & `fingerprint_seed.py`.
  - Added optional `fingerprint_seed` support to:
    - `launch_options()`
    - sync `NewContext()`
    - async `AsyncNewContext()`
    - `generate_context_fingerprint()`
    - BrowserForge generation/conversion
    - WebGL sampling
  - Supports `str`, `int`, and `bytes` seeds.
  - Rejects unsupported seed types such as `bool`.
  - Uses versioned, length-prefixed SHA-256 material to derive independent
  namespace-specific sub-seeds.
  - Keeps unseeded behavior random.
  - Ensures `fingerprint_seed` is consumed by Camoufox and not forwarded to
  Playwright.
  - Avoids unsupported context-level canvas setter calls in generated init
  scripts.
  - Adds a macOS `.app` bundle fallback for locating `properties.json`.

  ## Seeded Surfaces

  Seeded generation now covers Camoufox-owned generated values including:

  - BrowserForge sampling
  - preset selection
  - OS choice where applicable
  - WebGL sampling
  - font and voice subsets
  - screen offset sampling
  - `window.history.length`
  - audio/canvas/font spacing config seeds

  ## Compatibility / Caveats

  - Existing callers are unaffected unless they pass `fingerprint_seed`.
  - `fingerprint_seed` controls generated fingerprint values only.
  - It does not persist cookies, local storage, cache, or browser profile state.
  - Persistent state should still use a stable `user_data_dir` / persistent
  context.
  - Context-level seeds apply only to surfaces exposed by the current per-context
  init-script path.
  - This PR does not change TLS, proxy, network, or renderer-level behavior.

  ## Testing

  Regression tests added for:

  - deterministic seed derivation
  - namespace/type separation
  - invalid seed input handling
  - sync and async context API forwarding
  - deterministic launch config generation
  - deterministic context fingerprint generation
  - different seeds producing different noise values
  - unseeded launch/context paths remaining randomized
  - BrowserForge stability with concurrent seeded and unseeded calls
  - macOS app bundle `properties.json` fallback

  Local checks run:

  ```bash
  PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH=pythonlib python3 -m pytest
  --confcutdir=tests/patches tests/patches/fingerprint-seed.py tests/patches/
  context-api-seed.py tests/patches/context-fingerprint-seed.py tests/patches/
  launch-options-seed.py tests/patches/live-fingerprint-seed.py
```

  Result:

  18 passed, 2 skipped

  ## Dogfooding

  This branch is being dogfooded in VulpineOS for long-lived agent identities:

  - stable profile/account identifier -> fingerprint_seed
  - stable browser profile directory -> user_data_dir
  - generated Camoufox fingerprint values stay reproducible across restarts
  - cookies/storage/profile state remain handled separately by the persistent
    profile layer

title: Hide navigator.webdriver via [Pref] gate in WebIDL
body:
## Summary
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  `patches/playwright/1-leak-fixes.patch` already drops `Navigator::Webdriver()` to `return false` at the C++ level — but the `webdriver` attribute on `Navigator` is still **exposed** by WebIDL. Anti-bot platforms like FingerprintJS, DataDome and PerimeterX check the   *presence* of `navigator.webdriver`
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  ## Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  
  Two new hunks added to `1-leak-fixes.patch`:

title: Add config_overrides to generate_context_fingerprint(), fix font spacing disable
body:
Closes #600

Depends on #599 (test uses `helpers.py` added there).

This PR does two things because they're the same fix: font spacing perturbation can't be disabled because `generate_context_fingerprint()` doesn't let callers override config before init_script is rendered. The API addition (`config_overrides`) is the mechanism; disabling font spacing is the use case that proves it works.

## The problem

`generate_context_fingerprint()` builds the config dict and renders the init_script in one shot. The caller can't override config values before the init_script consumes them. Modifying `config['fonts:spacing_seed']` post-return doesn't work — `setFontSpacingSeed(12345)` is already baked into the JS string, and RoverfoxStorage (init_script) takes priority over MaskConfig (config dict) in `GetSeed()`.

This makes the `seed == 0` off-switch from #548 unreachable from Python. Most users don't hit this because they go through `AsyncNewContext()` (which doesn't expose config), but anyone calling `generate_context_fingerprint()` directly for sticky profiles, geo pinning, or per-session config has no way to override values before init_script rendering.

## The fix

New `config_overrides` kwarg — `dict.update()`'d into config after all building (preset, seeds, timezone, locale) but before `_build_init_script()`:

```python
fp = generate_context_fingerprint(
    preset=preset,
    config_overrides={'fonts:spacing_seed': 0},
)
# init_script now has setFontSpacingSeed(0) — perturbation disabled
# audio:seed and canvas:seed unaffected
```

## Design choice

The proper architecture would separate config building from init_script rendering — build config, let the caller modify it, then render explicitly. That's cleaner but breaking. `config_overrides` gives the same power without the API break, and the refactor remains open as a future direction.

## Regression risk

None. `config_overrides` defaults to `None` — when absent, the function behaves identically. No existing callers are affected.

## Testing

```
=== Test 1: config_overrides={'fonts:spacing_seed': 0} ===
  Measurements stable (all 319.08): PASS

=== Test 2: default (no overrides) gets non-zero seed ===
  Default seed is 607573064 (non-zero): PASS

=== Test 3: init_script emits setFontSpacingSeed(0) ===
  init_script contains setFontSpacingSeed(0): PASS

=== Test 4: audio/canvas seeds unaffected by font override ===
  audio:seed=3878680228, canvas:seed=781577443 (both non-zero): PASS

ALL TESTS PASSED
```

## Type of change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

title: No way to disable font spacing perturbation from Python (config overrides lost before init_script renders)
body:
`generate_context_fingerprint()` builds the config dict and renders the init_script internally. By the time the caller gets the return value, the JS init_script is already baked — modifying `config['fonts:spacing_seed']` post-return does nothing because `setFontSpacingSeed(12345)` is already in the rendered string, and RoverfoxStorage (init_script) takes priority over MaskConfig (config dict) in `GetSeed()`.

This makes the `seed == 0` off-switch from #548 unreachable from Python. The C++ guard works, but there's no way to get a 0 through the pipeline.

## Who hits this

Most users go through the high-level `AsyncNewContext()` wrapper, which calls `generate_context_fingerprint()` internally and doesn't expose config at all. They never need to override seeds — perturbation is always on, always random.

But anyone who calls `generate_context_fingerprint()` directly — which you need to do for sticky profiles (same seed → same fingerprint across sessions), geo pinning (timezone/locale from proxy exit IP), or per-session config control — has no way to override config values before the init_script is rendered. The low-level API is the right one for these use cases, but it lacks the override point.

## Why this matters

Font spacing perturbation produces synthetic glyph metrics — the LCG-shifted advances create font/canvas hashes outside the real-device population. Fingerprint checkers with population databases (e.g. PixelScan's "Masking detected" verdict, CreepJS `fonts.pixelSizeSystemSum`) flag these as synthetic. For sessions where plausibility matters more than inter-profile diversity, you need to be able to disable perturbation while keeping other seeds (audio, canvas) active. Currently impossible via the API.

## Suggested fix

Add a `config_overrides` dict parameter, applied after all config building but before init_script rendering:

```python
fp = generate_context_fingerprint(
    preset=preset,
    config_overrides={'fonts:spacing_seed': 0},
)
# init_script now has setFontSpacingSeed(0) — perturbation disabled
# audio:seed and canvas:seed unaffected
```

### Why not a cleaner API?

The proper fix would be separating config building from init_script rendering — return an intermediate config object, let the caller modify it, then render the init_script explicitly:

```python
config = build_fingerprint_config(preset=preset)
config['fonts:spacing_seed'] = 0
fp = render_fingerprint(config)
```

This is cleaner but breaking — `generate_context_fingerprint()` is the public API and callers depend on getting a fully-rendered result in one call. `config_overrides` gives the same power without the API break: overrides are applied in the right place (after config, before rendering), and the function signature stays backward-compatible (new optional kwarg, no positional changes).

The refactor remains a good future direction but isn't necessary for the immediate use case.

Happy to put up a PR if this looks reasonable.

title: Spoof system-ui font resolution to match target OS
body:
Closes #598

## Related Issue

#598 — `system-ui` CSS keyword resolves to platform font, leaking real OS

## Description

On Linux, the CSS generic keyword `system-ui` resolves via `LookAndFeel::GetFont(StyleSystemFont::Menu)` to the real GTK system font (`Sans`, `Ubuntu`, etc.). When spoofing macOS, this is a direct OS leak — CreepJS's `headless.systemFonts` catches it.

The existing font patches don't cover this path. `font-hijacker.patch` and `font-list-spoofing.patch` both operate on `FindAndAddFamiliesLocked`, which handles named font lookups. The `system-ui` generic keyword resolves through `ResolveGenericFontNames()` → `GetSystemUIFontFamilies()` — a separate code path that calls `LookAndFeel::GetFont` directly.

### The fix

Added an early return in `GetSystemUIFontFamilies()` that reads `navigator.platform` from MaskConfig (already set by the fingerprint) and returns the appropriate system font:

- `MacIntel` → `Helvetica`
- `Win32` → `Segoe UI`
- Linux / no config → falls through to real `LookAndFeel::GetFont` (no change)

No new config key — the fix co-varies with the existing fingerprint. If `navigator.platform` says macOS, `system-ui` resolves to Helvetica. No Python-side changes needed.

### Why these fonts

- **Helvetica**: macOS's sans-serif fallback. San Francisco (the actual system font) isn't available as a named font. Helvetica is in every macOS font list and what the bundled fontconfig maps `sans-serif` to.
- **Segoe UI**: Windows system font since Vista. Named and addressable.

### Verification

Canvas `measureText` with unquoted `system-ui` (the CSS generic keyword) now produces identical widths to `Helvetica` when spoofing macOS. Previously matched `Sans` (Linux leak).

Note: quoted `"system-ui"` in CSS is a literal font family name lookup — different code path, not affected by this patch. The unquoted form is what websites use and what CreepJS measures.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

title: system-ui CSS keyword resolves to platform font, leaking real OS
body:
## Bug

When spoofing macOS from Linux, the CSS generic keyword `system-ui` resolves to the real GTK system font (`Sans`, `Ubuntu`, etc.) instead of a macOS-plausible font. CreepJS detects this via `headless.systemFonts` — it renders text with `font-family: system-ui` and identifies the measured font as Linux-native.

All other font spoofing works: the font enumeration whitelist, font spacing seeds, per-context font lists. This is the last known font-level leak.

## Root cause

`system-ui` resolves through `ResolveGenericFontNames()` → `GetSystemUIFontFamilies()` in `gfx/thebes/gfxPlatformFontList.cpp`. That function calls `LookAndFeel::GetFont(StyleSystemFont::Menu)`, which on Linux queries the GTK theme and returns the real system font.

The existing font patches don't intercept this path:
- `font-hijacker.patch` sets a whitelist in the constructor — only affects named font lookups through `FindAndAddFamiliesLocked`
- `font-list-spoofing.patch` adds per-context filtering in `FindAndAddFamiliesLocked` — but `system-ui` bypasses it entirely, resolving through the generic family path

The bundled fontconfig (`fonts.conf`) maps `system-ui` → `"System Font"`, but `"System Font"` isn't a real installed font, so fontconfig falls back to `Sans`.

## Proposed fix

Intercept `GetSystemUIFontFamilies()` at the top — before `LookAndFeel::GetFont` — and read `navigator.platform` from MaskConfig to return the appropriate system font:
- `MacIntel` → `Helvetica`
- `Win32` → `Segoe UI`
- Anything else → fall through to real system font

No new config key needed — co-varies with the existing fingerprint automatically. Happy to put up a PR.

title: fix(virtdisplay): bug - race condition where multiple browsers get the same display
body:
## Summary

TLDR: 
[IMPORTANT BUG FIX] - existing code has race condition where multiple browsers get the same display if started at the same time => when one browser closes, the display is closed too => kills other live browser as well. Switching to the native and atomic displayfd makes way more sense, I'm surprised this wasn't the default method.  

AI description:
______________________________________________________________________________________________

Replace the userspace lock-file scan + random-jitter retry loop in `VirtualDisplay` with Xvfb's own `-displayfd` mechanism. Xvfb scans up from `:0` and atomically binds the first free X11 socket (kernel-mediated, no userspace race), then writes the chosen display number back through an inherited pipe.

This eliminates the duplicate-display race that occurred when many camoufox processes started concurrently and all observed the same set of free display numbers before any of them bound.

- Drops `multiprocessing.Lock` (only ever protected one process), `_get_lock_files`, `_free_display`.
- Adds a 10s read timeout on the displayfd pipe so a hung Xvfb fails fast instead of blocking forever.
- Forces software GLX (`__GLX_VENDOR_LIBRARY_NAME=mesa`, `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`) — Xvfb doesn't use the GPU, but on hosts with NVIDIA libGLvnd this avoids an rwlock stall on Xvfb startup.
- Detaches the child via `start_new_session=True` so a parent SIGINT doesn't propagate to Xvfb mid-bind.

This supersedes #595, which had a noisy force-push history from iterating on the prior lock-file approach.

## Test plan

New `pythonlib/tests/test_virtdisplay.py`

- [x] single launch returns `:N` and `kill()` actually terminates Xvfb
- [x] `get()` is idempotent within one `VirtualDisplay`
- [x] 50 concurrent `VirtualDisplay()` reservations all return unique displays (also verified locally at `VIRTDISPLAY_TEST_N=200`)
- [x] released display numbers can be reused on the next launch

```
$ cd pythonlib && python -m pytest tests/test_virtdisplay.py -v
tests/test_virtdisplay.py::test_single_launch_returns_valid_display_and_kill_terminates_xvfb PASSED
tests/test_virtdisplay.py::test_get_is_idempotent_within_one_virtual_display              PASSED
tests/test_virtdisplay.py::test_concurrent_reservations_all_get_unique_displays           PASSED
tests/test_virtdisplay.py::test_released_display_numbers_can_be_reused_on_the_next_launch PASSED
============================== 4 passed in 6.66s ==============================
```

The test directory is gitignored upstream (`pythonlib/test*`); a `!pythonlib/tests/` exception is added to keep new tests committable without unignoring the existing scratch test files.

title: fix(virtdisplay): atomic display claim + isolate per-launch DISPLAY env
body:
## Summary

Two related bugs broke `Camoufox(headless="virtual")` under parallel use in a single Python process:

1. **TOCTOU race in display claim.** `VirtualDisplay` previously scanned `/tmp/.X*-lock` to pick a "free" display number, then invoked Xvfb on `max(existing) + randint(3, 19)`. Two workers could read the same lock-file set, pick the same hint, and both invoke Xvfb on the same display. The losing Xvfb's `bind()` failed with "Server is already active", that worker silently ended up sharing the winner's Xvfb (or had no display at all).

2. **Shared `os.environ` mutation in the launch path.** `utils.py`'s launch helper aliased `env = os.environ` when no env was passed, then did `env['DISPLAY'] = virtual_display`. With multiple `Camoufox(headless="virtual")` calls running concurrently in one process, the last writer won — Firefox children inherited whatever `DISPLAY` happened to be live at the moment Playwright spawned them, causing some workers' browsers to die at startup pointing at another worker's Xvfb (or no Xvfb).

Both bugs are needed to make parallel launches reliable; either alone leaves a hole.

## Changes

### virtdisplay.py — atomic claim

Reserve the display number **before** spawning Xvfb, using a camoufox-private claim file that Xvfb itself never sees:

1. Compute a baseline above any existing `.X<N>-lock`.
2. For each candidate, skip if `.X<N>-lock` already exists.
3. `O_CREAT | O_EXCL` on `/tmp/.camoufox-X<N>.claim`. First-to-create wins; concurrent callers get `FileExistsError` and try the next number. Up to 50 attempts before raising `CannotExecuteXvfb`.
4. Write the owning PID into the claim file.
5. Spawn Xvfb on the reserved display.
6. Poll `/tmp/.X11-unix/X<N>` (the socket Xvfb only creates on a successful `bind()`) for up to 10s; raise `CannotExecuteXvfb` on timeout or early Xvfb exit.
7. On `kill()`, terminate Xvfb and unlink the claim file.

The claim file is intentionally separate from Xvfb's `.X<N>-lock` so Xvfb's own lock semantics (stale-PID detection, ownership, X.Org format) are untouched.

### virtdisplay.py — stale-claim recovery

If a camoufox process crashes before `kill()` runs, its claim file would leak and that display number would be permanently blocked. Every `_claim_display()` call sweeps `/tmp/.camoufox-X*.claim` first:

- Read the PID from each claim file. `kill(pid, 0)` raising `ProcessLookupError` → owner is dead → unlink.
- Unreadable / malformed claim files (which can briefly appear during the window between `O_CREAT` and the PID being written) are tolerated for a 5-second grace period before being treated as stale, so a concurrent sweep cannot unlink a live in-progress claim.
- Claim files whose PID is owned by another user (`PermissionError`) are left alone.

### utils.py — copy `os.environ` instead of aliasing

`launch_options(...)` now does `env = dict(environ)` instead of `env = environ`, so per-call `env['DISPLAY'] = virtual_display` writes don't leak across concurrent launches in the same process.

### virtdisplay.py — force Mesa software GLX on Xvfb

While here: set `__GLX_VENDOR_LIBRARY_NAME=mesa` and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1` in Xvfb's spawn env. On hosts with NVIDIA drivers installed, libGLvnd loads NVIDIA's GLX provider, which acquires a global rwlock during GL init that can stall Xvfb startup for several seconds under concurrent GPU contention. Xvfb on `1x1x24` never renders anything GPU-accelerated, so software GLX is strictly an improvement.

## Why not `-displayfd`

An earlier revision used Xvfb's own `-displayfd` (let Xvfb's kernel-side `bind()` race auto-increment past collisions, read the chosen number on a pipe). It worked but had two drawbacks:

1. Every spawn paid Xvfb startup cost even on collision (Xvfb forks, retries internally, then reports).
2. The pipe-read with timeout adds startup-path failure modes (EOF, timeout, unparseable output) that need handling and made hangs harder to diagnose.

The claim-file approach resolves contention before `fork()`, so a colliding worker just retries an `os.open()` instead of waiting on a Xvfb spawn.

## Testing

Verified locally on Linux with Xvfb 21.1.11 on a host with NVIDIA drivers (where the latent libGLvnd issue exists). Test suite covers:

**virtdisplay claim correctness**

- 16 threads claiming displays simultaneously → 16 unique displays, 0 errors
- 16 processes claiming displays simultaneously → 16 unique displays, 0 errors
- 8 real Xvfb instances spawned in parallel (0.89s) → 8 distinct live displays, all responsive to `xdpyinfo`
- Single-display lifecycle → spawn, `xdpyinfo` confirms X.Org responding, `kill()` removes both the X11 socket and the claim file

**Stale-claim recovery (5 sub-cases)**

- Claim file with a dead PID is unlinked by the sweep
- Claim file with a live PID is preserved
- Subprocess claims a display, "crashes" without cleanup; next sweep reclaims the slot
- Malformed claim file is preserved within the 5s grace window, removed after
- Normal claim contains the owning PID and is removed by `kill()`

**End-to-end parallel `Camoufox(headless="virtual")`**

Before the env fix: ~25-30% of workers in N=4 batches failed with `Target page closed` / `BrowserType.launch failed` because their Firefox children inherited another worker's `DISPLAY`.

After the fix:

- 8 rounds × N=4 → 32/32 success
- N=8 → 8/8 success in 7.4s
- N=12 → 12/12 success in 8.5s

title: fix(juggler): bug - exact-edge mousemoves hang, filepicker events not properly emitted
body:
## Summary

Re-submission of #580, narrowed to a single commit so it can land on its own. Two small juggler fixes:

- **Filepicker event**: re-anchor the patch hunk so the filepicker emit lands in the right location relative to upstream `HTMLInputElement::InitFilePicker`. The previous offset put the hunk in the wrong function and the event wasn't being dispatched.
- **Edge mousemove hang**: in `PageHandler.dispatchMouseEvent`, treat coordinates exactly at the right/bottom edge (`x == width` or `y == height`) as out-of-viewport. At those exact coordinates Firefox fires `eMouseExitFromWidget` instead of `eMouseMove`, so the per-event `juggler-mouse-event-hit-renderer` observer notification never arrives and every later input event hangs behind it indefinitely.

Boundary check changes from `>` to `>=` for width/height, matching the half-open viewport convention.

#580 is being closed in favor of this one + a separate virtdisplay PR.

## Test plan

- [x] Trigger a file input in a Playwright/juggler script — `filechooser` event fires reliably
- [x] Drive a mousemove to coordinates exactly at the viewport edge — subsequent input events still complete instead of hanging

Verified fix In my own build - https://github.com/JWriter20/camoufox/releases/tag/v146.0.1-beta.25.2

## Related Issue Closes #591 ## Description Adds a Juggler `Page` domain method that exposes Firefox's `nsIEventListenerService.getListenerInfoFor(node)` so Juggler clients can enumerate the event listeners attached to a DOM node. ### Motivation The recent surge of LLM-agent browser tooling (Browser-Use, chrome-devtools-mcp, Vercel agent-browser, browserbase, and others) all need to discover non-ARIA interactive elements like `
` or `` to drive realistic agent ↔ web interactions. Pure accessibility-tree walks miss those — the AX tree marks them as `role=generic`, so the agent sees a static page when the user sees a clickable surface. Chrome has long exposed `getEventListeners(el)` in the DevTools Runtime context for this case; this patch brings parity to Firefox-flavored automation through Juggler. ### Diff scope (~60 lines, three files) **`additions/juggler/protocol/Protocol.js`** - New `pageTypes.EventListenerInfo` type. Field names mirror `nsIEventListenerInfo` verbatim (`capturing`, `allowsUntrusted`, `inSystemEventGroup`) so the mapping from the underlying XPCOM service is unambiguous. The DOM-level `passive` flag is intentionally omitted because Firefox doesn't expose it through this interface. - New `'getEventListenersForNode'` method on the Page domain, adjacent to `describeNode` since both are node-introspection. **`additions/juggler/protocol/PageHandler.js`** - One-line dispatch from `Page.getEventListenersForNode` to the content-side handler, mirroring `Page.describeNode`. **`additions/juggler/content/PageAgent.js`** - Register `getEventListenersForNode` in the `browserChannel` method table. - Implement `_getEventListenersForNode({objectId, frameId})` using `frame.unsafeObject(objectId)` (same pattern as `_describeNode` / `_getContentQuads`), then project each `nsIEventListenerInfo` into the wire shape. The XPCOM service this wraps is stable since 2008 (bug 524674) and the patch is purely additive — no existing methods or types are touched. ## Type of Change - [ ] Bug fix - [x] New feature - [ ] Documentation update - [ ] Other ## Testing Built Camoufox 146.0.1-beta.25 from source on Linux x86_64 (`make fetch && make setup && BUILD_TARGET=linux,x86_64 make build`, exit 0 in ~28 min wall-clock). title: Add Page.getEventListenersForNode to the Juggler protocol
body:
### Describe the feature:

Add a new Juggler `Page` domain method that enumerates the event listeners attached to a DOM node, by wrapping the existing `nsIEventListenerService.getListenerInfoFor(node)` XPCOM service:

```
Page.getEventListenersForNode({ frameId, objectId })
  → { listeners: [
        { type, capturing, allowsUntrusted, inSystemEventGroup },
        ...
      ]
    }
```

Field names mirror Firefox's `nsIEventListenerInfo` interface (`dom/events/nsIEventListenerService.idl`) verbatim so the mapping from the underlying XPCOM service is unambiguous. The DOM-level `passive` flag is intentionally omitted because Firefox does not expose it through this interface.

The patch is purely additive — no existing methods or types are touched. ~60 lines across three files in `additions/juggler/`:

- `protocol/Protocol.js` — declare the method + add `pageTypes.EventListenerInfo`
- `protocol/PageHandler.js` — one-line dispatch to the content side
- `content/PageAgent.js` — register + implement via `nsIEventListenerService`

I have a working patch (verified locally on Camoufox 146.0.1-beta.25 — Protocol.js validation accepts the new schema, the build runs cleanly, and the wire stack accepts Juggler messages with the patch in place) and will open a PR linking this issue.

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

The recent surge of LLM-agent browser tooling — Browser-Use, chrome-devtools-mcp, Vercel's agent-browser, browserbase, and others — all need to discover non-ARIA interactive elements like `<div onclick>` or `<span data-action>` to drive realistic agent ↔ web interactions. Pure accessibility-tree walks miss these elements: the AX tree marks them as `role=generic`, so the agent sees a static page when the user sees a clickable surface.

Chrome's DevTools Runtime context has long exposed a `getEventListeners(el)` helper for exactly this case; bringing parity to Firefox-flavored automation through Juggler closes the gap and makes Camoufox a viable backend for agent stacks that today only target Chromium.

The XPCOM service this wraps is stable since 2008 (https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=524674). Adding the binding is a thin, low-risk change.

title: feat: Obscura integration — challenge-solver flag
body:
## Problem

Obscura needs a way to delegate captcha/anti-bot challenges to the Camoufox solver service.

## Proposal

Add to Obscura CLI:
```bash
obscura fetch https://seace.gob.pe/... \
  --challenge-solver http://localhost:8888 \
  --eval "document.title"
```

### Flow
1. Obscura loads page
2. Detects challenge (reCAPTCHA script, Cloudflare headers, etc.)
3. Calls solver service: `POST http://localhost:8888/solve`
4. Receives token/cookies
5. Injects into page and continues

### Detection heuristics
- `<script src="*recaptcha*">` → recaptcha_v3
- `<script src="*challenges.cloudflare*">` → turnstile
- `cf-mitigated: challenge` header → cloudflare_waf
- Title "Just a moment..." → cloudflare_waf

title: feat: Cloudflare Turnstile and WAF solver
body:
## Problem

Cloudflare Turnstile and WAF 5-second challenges block automated access. Need real browser to solve them and return session cookies.

## Solution

### Turnstile
1. Navigate to page with Turnstile widget
2. Wait for challenge to auto-solve (Camoufox passes fingerprint checks)
3. Extract cf_clearance cookie and turnstile token

### WAF 5s Challenge  
1. Navigate to Cloudflare challenge page
2. Wait for redirect after challenge passes
3. Return cf_clearance + __cf_bm cookies

## API

```json
POST /solve
{
  "type": "cloudflare_waf",
  "url": "https://protected-site.com"
}

Response:
{
  "cookies": {"cf_clearance": "...", "__cf_bm": "..."},
  "user_agent": "Mozilla/5.0...",
  "solve_time_ms": 6500
}
```

title: feat: reCAPTCHA v3 solver using Camoufox
body:
## Problem

reCAPTCHA v3 tokens generated via HTTP-only have low scores (~0.1). Sites like SEACE validate scores server-side and reject low-score tokens silently.

## Solution

Use Camoufox (real browser with 0% detection) to:
1. Navigate to the target page
2. Wait for reCAPTCHA script to load
3. Execute `grecaptcha.execute(sitekey, {action})` 
4. Capture the generated token (high score ~0.7-0.9)
5. Return token to caller

## API

```json
POST /solve
{
  "type": "recaptcha_v3",
  "url": "https://prod2.seace.gob.pe/...",
  "sitekey": "6Lfhnb0pAAAAA...",
  "action": "search"
}

Response:
{
  "token": "03AFcWeA4...",
  "score": 0.9,
  "solve_time_ms": 3200
}
```

title: feat: Add browser pool manager for concurrent solving
body:
## Problem

Each solve request currently requires launching a new browser instance (~2-3s startup). For high-throughput solving, we need a pool of pre-warmed browser instances.

## Proposal

- Pool of 4-8 Camoufox browser instances (configurable)
- Instances are reused across requests (with context isolation)
- Auto-recycle after N uses or on error
- Queue system for requests when pool is full
- Health monitoring per instance

## Config

```
POOL_SIZE=4
MAX_USES_PER_INSTANCE=50
INSTANCE_TIMEOUT=300
```

title: feat: Add HTTP API solver service for captcha/anti-bot bypass
body:
## Proposal

Add a FastAPI-based HTTP service (`service/`) that exposes Camoufox browser capabilities as a REST API for solving captchas and bypassing anti-bot protections.

## Motivation

Lightweight headless browsers (like Obscura) can handle 90% of scraping but fail on sites with reCAPTCHA v3, Cloudflare Turnstile, or WAF challenges. These need a real browser with proper fingerprinting. Camoufox is perfect for this but lacks an API service layer.

## Architecture

```
Client (Obscura/curl/any)     Camoufox Solver Service
POST /solve ──────────────>  Pool of Camoufox browsers
{type, url, sitekey}         Solves challenge
                <────────── Returns {token, cookies, headers}
GET /health ──────────────>  Status check
```

## Endpoints

- `POST /solve` — Solve a challenge (recaptcha_v3, turnstile, cloudflare_waf)
- `GET /health` — Service health + pool status
- `GET /session` — Get pre-authenticated session cookies for a URL

## Components needed

1. `service/app.py` — FastAPI application
2. `service/pool.py` — Browser pool manager (create/reuse/recycle instances)
3. `service/solvers/recaptcha_v3.py` — reCAPTCHA v3 solver
4. `service/solvers/turnstile.py` — Cloudflare Turnstile solver
5. `service/solvers/cloudflare_waf.py` — Cloudflare WAF/5s challenge solver
6. `service/Dockerfile` — Container deployment
7. Integration docs for Obscura

title: fix: FF146 issues - don't crash on mousemove on page edge, properly emit filepicker event
body:
## Related Issue
N/A

## Description

This PR contains two small bug fixes that occur when using camoufox with firefox v146.0.1:

1. **File picker event handling is broken.** The patch hunk that wires up file-input interception had stale line numbers (`@@ -799`), so when Firefox's `HTMLInputElement.cpp` shifted, the patch no longer matched and the interception code never made it into the build. As a result, when clicking on a filepicker, the associated event isn't actually sent. Fix: update the hunk header to the current location (`@@ -848`). No code logic changed — just the location markers the patch tool uses to find the spot.

2. **Mouse events at the exact viewport edge permanently freeze the page.** When automation dispatches a mousemove at coordinates exactly on the edge (`x == width` or `y == height`), Firefox's widget layer treats it as an exit/leave event rather than `eMouseMove`. Camoufox waits for a "renderer received the mousemove" signal that never fires for exit events, so `sendEvents()` awaits forever, deadlocks `activateAndRun`'s global chain, and every subsequent `Input.*` call queues behind it for the rest of the page's life. Fix: treat exact-edge coordinates the same as out-of-viewport coordinates by changing `>` to `>=` in the bounds check, so they take the existing out-of-viewport fallback path.

This is not related to: https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/commit/873618e45406f73bb27fec222e42bcc2a292af1f which was a separate issue also leading to a mousemove crash.

I faced both issues previously and confirmed both are resolved after rebuilding the binary.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Other

## Testing

**File picker fix:**
1. Build Camoufox from this branch.
2. Click on a `<input type="file">` element with a listener for the firepicker event.
3. Expected: the event is received and we can attach the file.

**Viewport-edge mousemove fix:**
1. Open any page with a viewport of known size (e.g. 1280×720).
2. Dispatch a mousemove at `(1280, 360)` or `(640, 720)` — exactly on the right or bottom edge.
3. Then dispatch any further input event (click, key, mousemove).
4. Expected: subsequent events run normally. Before this fix, the page would stop responding to all input events from that point on.

## Fingerprint Report

Please submit a report from both the service tester and build tester.

I was getting an issue, Failed to generate presets: Command failed: python3 '/var/task/scripts/generate-presets.py' /bin/sh: line 1: python3: command not found Is the camoufox Python package installed? Run: pip install camoufox. 

</details>

title: Camoufox silently fails Turnstile inside Docker container

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

body:
## Summary
Cloudflare Turnstile silently fails when Camoufox runs inside a Docker container, regardless of browser version or configuration. The Turnstile widget is detected but the interactive challenge cannot be solved — the success element never appears. This does **not** occur when running on the host machine.

I understand this is a duplicate of #311. However, due to the age of that issue, and the fact that there is work being done to enhance hardware spoofing, I thought it worth to open a new issue and provide fresh data.

## Environment
- **Container**: Docker on Linux (aarch64), browser runs headless via Xvfb
- **Camoufox**: Tested with multiple browser versions and library forks (v135, v142, v146)
- **Turnstile solver**: `playwright-captcha` ClickSolver
## Symptoms
1. Page rendering works correctly — HTML is fully rendered, forms are visible, inputs fill correctly
2. Turnstile widget is detected on the page
3. ClickSolver fails with: `CaptchaDetectionError: Cloudflare turnstile success element does not exist on the page.`
4. After the solver attempt, the widget is removed from the DOM, but the response token is rejected by Cloudflare
5. The site shows: "Captcha failed, try to reload."
## Known Camoufox Issues
### v146 Brotli Decompression Bug
Camoufox v146 prerelease has broken Brotli decompression — HTTP responses with `content-encoding: br` are rendered as raw binary garbage. Pages show 0 inputs, 0 buttons, 0 forms.
**Workaround**: Set `"headers.Accept-Encoding": "gzip, deflate"` in the Camoufox config to prevent Brotli responses. However, omitting `br` from `Accept-Encoding` may itself be a bot detection signal, as most real browsers include it.
### Xvfb 1×1 Screen Size
Camoufox spawns Xvfb with `-screen 0 1x1x24`, a 1×1 pixel virtual screen. This is a well-known bot detection signal — real browsers never have a 1×1 screen.
**Workaround**: Patch `VirtualDisplay.xvfb_args` at runtime:
```python
from camoufox.virtdisplay import VirtualDisplay
VirtualDisplay.xvfb_args = tuple(
    a.replace("1x1x24", "1920x1080x24") if "1x1x24" in a else a
    for a in VirtualDisplay.xvfb_args
)
```
### repos.yml Version Filter
`repos.yml` ships with `min: "beta.19"` which excludes alpha prereleases (v146+). The `__version__.py` has `MIN_VERSION="alpha.1"`, creating a mismatch.
**Fix**: Patch `repos.yml` at build time: `sed -i 's/min: "beta\.19"/min: "alpha.1"/'`
### fontconfigs Symlink
v146 bundles `fontconfig/` but the Python library expects `fontconfigs/`.
**Fix**: `ln -sf fontconfig "$BROWSER_DIR/fontconfigs"`
## Test Matrix
| Browser Version | Brotli | Page Rendering | Turnstile |
|----------------|--------|---------------|-----------|
| v135 (stable) | ✅ native | ✅ | ❌ fails |
| v142 (CoryKing fork) | ✅ native | ✅ | ❌ fails |
| v146 (prerelease) | ❌ broken | ✅ with workaround | ❌ fails |

Turnstile fails consistently across all versions — the issue is not browser-specific.

### ✅ Multiple Camoufox Libraries Tested
- `camoufox` 0.4.12 (CoryKing fork — v142 browser)
- `camoufox` 0.5.0 (daijro — v146 prerelease)
- `cloverlabs-camoufox` 0.5.5 (CloverLabs — v146 prerelease)

All produce the same result: Turnstile widget detected but solver fails.

RUN python -m playwright install chromium
RUN python -m camoufox fetch

COPY --chown=someuser:someuser ./src /app
WORKDIR /app
```
```yaml
# ./docker-compose.yaml

networks:
  some_network:

services:
  scraper:
    command:
      - python
      - /app/scrape.py
    networks:
      - some_network
    volumes:
      - ./src:/app
    working_dir: /app
    container_name: scraper
    # Replicate readonly environment in pods for more reliable testing.
    read_only: true
    tmpfs:
      - /tmp
    image: scraper:latest
```
```python
# ./src/scrape.py

import asyncio
from functools import lru_cache

from scrapling.engines.toolbelt.custom import Response as ScraplingResponse


@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def get_stealthy_fetcher():
    from scrapling.fetchers import StealthyFetcher

    return StealthyFetcher



async def scrape(the_url: str):
    try:
        page: ScraplingResponse = await get_stealthy_fetcher().async_fetch(
            the_url, headless=True, network_idle=True
        )
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"Fetch failed for URL <{the_url}>: <{exc}>")
        return
    if not page:
        print(f"Fetch returned empty page for URL <{the_url}>.")
        return
    if page.status != 200:
        print(f"Fetch status code for URL <{the_url}> is not 200.")
        return
    return page.body


def main():
    out = asyncio.run(scrape("https://example.com/"))
    if out:
        print(out[:100])
    else:
        print("No out")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

Then run:
```bash
docker build . -t scraper:latest
docker compose up
```


### Version:
```bash
$ poetry run python -m camoufox version
Pip package:	v0.4.11
Camoufox:	v135.0.1-beta.24 (Up to date!)
```
Moreover:
```bash
$ poetry run python -V
Python 3.12.2
$ poetry run pip freeze | grep -e camou -e playwri -e scrapling
camoufox==0.4.11
playwright==1.58.0
scrapling==0.3.9
```

### Debugging

One approach I've had was to run `inotify` with disabled `read_only` in `docker-compose.yaml` like
```bash
inotifywait -m -r --timefmt '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S' --format '%T %w %f %e' / >> ~/changes.log
```
and run a Python script to fetch an URL through `scrapling`. After that I told AI to sum it up for me.
Beside operations on `/tmp` and `/dev` it confirmed writes to `~/.cache/fontconfig` and an unnecessary read-write opening of the [webgl/webgl_data.db](https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/blob/main/pythonlib/camoufox/webgl/webgl_data.db) SQLite3 database by [webgl/sample.py](https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/blob/main/pythonlib/camoufox/webgl/sample.py) which surprisingly didn't blew in the read-only directory. I called it "unnecessary" because not a single query in that file modified the database and opening it with default read-write mode wasn't needed.
For some reason operation that was the main culprit wasn't present in that file. Maybe I did something wrong but I've tried something else.

Thing that helped was `strace` of the launched command mentioned in the logs:
```bash
strace -e trace=openat,creat,mkdir,mkdirat -f ~/.cache/camoufox/camoufox-bin -no-remote -headless -profile /tmp/path/doesnt/matter -juggler-pipe about:blank 2>&1 | grep "EACCES\|EROFS\|EPERM"
```

To replicate it in your env run:
```bash
$ docker compose up
# run in another terminal:
$ docker exec -it scraper bash
$ strace ... # inside the container
```

Again `~/.cache/fontconfig` was mentioned (and sometimes `/var/cache/fontconfig` or `~/.fontconfig`) but this was also present:
```bash
[pid    26] mkdir("~/.camoufox", 0700) = -1 EROFS (Read-only file system)
```
I've almost missed it because it looked almost like `~/.cache/camoufox` and it was a just a single line. But I finally nailed it.

### Solution

Based on the above debugging steps I've found the solution for my particular case but I don't know if it is addressable from just library installation through `pip` or running `camoufox fetch`.

What is needed but not obvious and was very hard to find without `strace`:
```Dockerfile
# Dockerfile

RUN mkdir ~/.camoufox
```
Yes. That's literally it. This directory doesn't even need to be writable it just has to exists.
Without it existing before running, `camoufox-bin` tries to create it and fails silently in read-only environment.

Other thing that can be done to reduce errors during startup is this:
```yaml
    tmpfs:
      ...
      - ~/.cache/fontconfig
```
but this is optional.

That just for local `docker compose`.

In case of read-only GKE pod and helm charts I've had to:
1. "install" all things that go into `~/.cache/camoufox` to other directory (lets call it `/opt/camoufox`)
2. create `extraVolumes > emptyDir: {}` for each `extraVolumeMounts > readOnly: true` with `mountPath` for `~/.cache/camoufox` and `~/.cache/fontconfig`
3. add `initContainers` entry like this
```yaml
- name: camoufox-cache-init
  command: ["cp", "-rT", "/opt/camoufox", "~/.cache/camoufox"]
  volumeMounts:
    - name: camoufox-cache
      mountPath: ~/.cache/camoufox
  ....

```

---

I've made it so long to give some hints with debugging such silent errors in read-only environments for binaries with improper error handling/logging.

I've used `~` instead of full `/home/someuser` in examples above - adjust accordingly to your needs.

title: Fix out-of-viewport mousemove crash (sendMouseEvent → jugglerSendMouseEvent)
body:
Closes #564

## Summary

One-line fix: `PageHandler.js` calls `sendMouseEvent()` for out-of-viewport mousemoves, but this method doesn't exist on `nsIDOMWindowUtils`. Should be `jugglerSendMouseEvent()` — matching the in-viewport code path on line 511 and `PageAgent.js` line 542.

## Description

When `Page.dispatchMouseEvent` receives a mousemove with coordinates outside the viewport, it takes a special path (line 540) to move the mouse off the web content and clear hover effects. This path calls `win.windowUtils.sendMouseEvent()`, which throws because the method doesn't exist in Firefox's DOM API.

The in-viewport path correctly uses `jugglerSendMouseEvent()` — the Playwright-specific extension added to `nsIDOMWindowUtils`. The out-of-viewport fallback just has the wrong method name.

Triggers during normal automation when interacting with elements near the viewport edge — date pickers, dropdowns, drag operations.

title: Out-of-viewport mousemove crashes: sendMouseEvent is not a function
body:
## Problem

`Page.dispatchMouseEvent` in PageHandler.js crashes when the mouse moves outside the viewport:

```
Mouse.move: Protocol error (Page.dispatchMouseEvent): win.windowUtils.sendMouseEvent is not a function
```

This happens during normal automation when interacting with elements near the viewport edge (date pickers, dropdowns, tooltips). The browser session becomes unusable after the error.

## Root cause

`PageHandler.js` line 548 calls `win.windowUtils.sendMouseEvent()` for out-of-viewport mousemoves, but this method doesn't exist on `nsIDOMWindowUtils`. It was never part of the Firefox API.

The in-viewport code path (line 511) correctly uses `win.windowUtils.jugglerSendMouseEvent()`, which is the Playwright-added extension. `PageAgent.js` line 542 also uses the correct method. Only the out-of-viewport fallback in `PageHandler.js` has the wrong name.

## Fix

One-line change: `sendMouseEvent` → `jugglerSendMouseEvent` at PageHandler.js line 548. PR incoming.

title: Add timezone and locale parameters to generate_context_fingerprint()
body:
Closes #559

## Description

`generate_context_fingerprint()` and `launch_options()` don't coordinate on timezone and locale. Geoip resolves these in `launch_options()`, but the init script is already baked by `generate_context_fingerprint()`. There's no way to pass pre-resolved timezone/locale into the fingerprint.

### The fix

**`fingerprints.py`**: New `timezone` and `locale` params on `generate_context_fingerprint()`. When provided, injected into config before init_script generation. Locale parsed via `normalize_locale()` into `locale:language`, `locale:region`, `navigator.language`. Also sets `context_options['locale']` and `context_options['timezone_id']`.

**`utils.py`**: In `launch_options()`, geoip timezone/locale keys now use `setdefault` instead of blind overwrite. Pre-set values aren't clobbered; geolocation coordinates still overwrite (they're per-session).

### Design note

This is somewhat opinionated — it fits workflows where one IP maps to one-or-more profiles, and a profile is never used with a different IP (identity consistency across sessions). Entirely opt-in: callers who don't pass these params get current behaviour.

## Type of change

- [x] New feature

## Backward compatibility

Fully backward compatible. Both params default to `None`. The `setdefault` change only matters when config keys are already present.

title: Add media:spoof_codecs config option to prevent codec fingerprinting
body:
Closes #558

## Description

`canPlayType()` and `MediaSource.isTypeSupported()` leak which system codec libraries are installed by querying `PDMFactory::Supports()`. Different environments → different codec support → fingerprintable. CreepJS detects this as mismatched `media.mimeTypes`.

### The fix

New `media:spoof_codecs` config key. When enabled, bypasses `PDMFactory::Supports()` in `MP4Decoder::IsSupportedType()` and `MatroskaDecoder::IsSupportedType()` — reports all valid codec strings as supported regardless of system decoders.

```json
{ "media:spoof_codecs": true }
```

Default `false` — standard behaviour unchanged.

### Trade-off

The browser claims codec support even when no actual decoder is present. `canPlayType("video/mp4; codecs=hev1...")` → `"probably"` even without HEVC. Actual playback fails at decode time, not query time. Correct trade-off for anti-fingerprinting; users who need real playback should only enable this with matching decoders installed.

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature

title: Set FONTCONFIG_FILE to isolate bundled fonts on Linux
body:
Closes #557

## Description

On Linux, system fonts leak into the rendering pipeline. The font enumeration whitelist hides system fonts from JavaScript, but fontconfig still loads them as rendering fallbacks. This makes datacenter machines trivially identifiable — a minimal cloud VM has ~4 font packages vs ~120 on a desktop, producing measurably different canvas fingerprints, font metrics, and SVG rendering.

**Root cause**: `get_env_vars()` computes the bundled fontconfig path, validates `fonts.conf` exists, then discards it without setting `FONTCONFIG_FILE`. Fontconfig defaults to `/etc/fonts/fonts.conf` and loads system fonts.

### The fix

Added `_generate_fontconfig()` that reads the bundled `fonts.conf`, replaces the relative `<dir prefix="cwd">fonts</dir>` with an absolute path (resolved at runtime), writes a content-hashed copy to `~/.cache/camoufox/fontconfig/`, and sets `FONTCONFIG_FILE`.

Same Camoufox build + same profile: CreepJS `pixelSizeSystemSum`, `textMetricsSystemSum`, `fontFaceLoadFonts` now identical between GCP VM and residential Linux.

macOS and Windows unaffected (gated on `OS_NAME == 'lin'`).

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

title: Fix init_script timezone poisoning (companion to #546)
body:
Closes #556. Companion to #546.

## Description

When no explicit timezone is provided at fingerprint generation time (the standard `geoip=True` flow), the init script falls back to `setTimezone(Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone)` — reading the host's system timezone and storing it in `RoverfoxStorageManager`. This poisons the storage before the MaskConfig fallback from #546 can fire.

On a GCP VM (UTC) with a UK proxy: workers report UTC instead of Europe/London.

### The fix

Remove the `else` branch in `_build_init_script()`. When no explicit timezone is provided, don't call `setTimezone()` at all. The C++ `SetNewDocument()` hook and `TimezoneManager::GetTimezone()` MaskConfig fallback from #546 handle timezone propagation correctly when the init script doesn't interfere.

### How it interacts with #546

| PR | Side | What it fixes |
|---|---|---|
| #546 | C++ | `GetTimezone()` falls back to MaskConfig when storage is empty |
| This | Python | Init script no longer poisons storage, so the fallback actually fires |

Neither fix is sufficient alone.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

title: generate_context_fingerprint() has no way to set timezone or locale
body:
`generate_context_fingerprint()` and `launch_options()` don't coordinate on timezone and locale. Geoip resolves these in `launch_options()`, but the init script is already baked by `generate_context_fingerprint()` before geoip runs. There's no way to pass pre-resolved timezone/locale to the fingerprint generator.

This matters for profile-persistence workflows: resolve geoip once for a proxy IP, pin the timezone/locale, reuse across sessions without re-resolving. Currently there's no clean API for this — timezone only enters the fingerprint if the preset includes it (most don't), and locale has no path in at all.

## Proposed fix

1. Add `timezone` and `locale` params to `generate_context_fingerprint()` — injected into config before init_script generation
2. In `launch_options()`, use `setdefault` for geoip timezone/locale keys so pre-set values aren't overwritten

This is somewhat opinionated — it fits workflows where one IP maps to one-or-more profiles, and a profile is never used with a different IP. Opt-in: callers who don't pass these params get current behaviour.

title: canPlayType() and isTypeSupported() leak system codec libraries
body:
`canPlayType()` and `MediaSource.isTypeSupported()` reveal which system codec libraries are installed. Different environments have different FFmpeg versions or VideoToolbox availability, so these APIs return different results for the same browser profile. CreepJS flags this as differing `media.mimeTypes`.

A Linux server with FFmpeg 6.x spoofing a macOS profile still reports a Linux-server codec matrix. Easy correlation signal.

## Root cause

`MP4Decoder::IsSupportedType()` and `MatroskaDecoder::IsSupportedType()` call `PDMFactory::Supports()` which enumerates actual system decoders. Useful for playback decisions, but leaks the host's codec stack to any page that asks.

## Proposed fix

Add a `media:spoof_codecs` config key. When enabled, short-circuit `IsSupportedType()` to return `true` for any valid codec string without consulting `PDMFactory`. Trade-off: claims support for codecs that may not decode. Fine for fingerprint resistance; opt-in so default behaviour is unchanged.

title: System fonts leak into rendering pipeline on Linux — FONTCONFIG_FILE never set
body:
On Linux, system fonts leak into the font rendering fallback chain. The font *enumeration* whitelist (font-hijacker.patch) hides system fonts from JavaScript, but fontconfig still loads them for rendering fallback — emoji, CJK, mathematical symbols, anything not in the bundled fonts. The rendered pixels differ, and any metric that measures glyph rendering picks up the difference.

This makes datacenter machines trivially identifiable. A minimal cloud VM has ~4 font packages; a desktop Linux box has ~120. Canvas fingerprinting, `pixelSizeSystemSum`, `textMetricsSystemSum` all diverge — even with the same Camoufox build, same profile, same proxy.

## Root cause

`get_env_vars()` in `utils.py` computes the path to the bundled `fonts.conf`, validates it exists, then **discards it without setting `FONTCONFIG_FILE`**. Without this env var, fontconfig loads `/etc/fonts/fonts.conf` which pulls in system font directories.

The bundled `fonts.conf` even says "This file sets Tor Browser's bundled fonts as the only available system fonts" — but that intent was never enforced.

Secondary issue: the bundled config uses `<dir prefix="cwd">fonts</dir>` — relative to browser CWD, which Playwright doesn't guarantee. Needs rewriting to an absolute path at runtime.

## Proposed fix

After validating `fonts.conf`, read it, replace the relative `<dir>` with an absolute path to the bundled fonts, write to a cached location, and set `FONTCONFIG_FILE`. Happy to put up a PR — already working locally.

title: Init script timezone fallback poisons storage, blocking MaskConfig resolution
body:
When `generate_context_fingerprint()` runs before geoip resolves (the normal flow), the init script falls back to `setTimezone(Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone)` — reading the host's system timezone and storing it in `RoverfoxStorageManager`. This poisons the storage.

When `AsyncCamoufox(geoip=...)` later resolves the correct timezone from the proxy IP into `CAMOU_CONFIG`, workers already have the wrong value from storage. The MaskConfig fallback from #546 is never consulted because storage isn't empty.

On a GCP VM (UTC) proxied through a UK residential IP, workers report UTC instead of Europe/London.

## Root cause

```
generate_context_fingerprint()  →  init_script baked with system TZ fallback
AsyncCamoufox(geoip=...)        →  CAMOU_CONFIG gets "Europe/London"
Browser starts                  →  init_script runs first, calls setTimezone("UTC")
Workers                         →  read "UTC" from storage, MaskConfig fallback never fires
```

The `else` branch in `_build_init_script()` was meant to trigger self-destruct on `setTimezone()`, but storing the system timezone is actively harmful.

## Proposed fix

Remove the `else` branch. When no explicit timezone is provided, don't call `setTimezone()` at all — let the C++ MaskConfig path from #546 handle it. Python-side companion to #546.

title: Akamai-protected sites block Camoufox but not stock Firefox via Playwright
body:
### Akamai-protected sites block Camoufox but not stock Firefox via Playwright

**What happens:**
Navigating to Akamai-protected sites (e.g. `https://www.hilton.com`) with Camoufox returns 403, while stock Firefox via the same Playwright protocol loads the page normally.

**Expected behavior:**
The page should load normally, as it does with stock Firefox via the same Playwright protocol.

**Key finding — detection is NOT TLS/HTTP2:**
Both stock Firefox and Camoufox produce **identical** TLS and HTTP/2 fingerprints:

| Signal | Stock Firefox (Playwright) | Camoufox |
|---|---|---|
| JA3 | `6f7889b9fb1a62a9577e685c1fcfa919` | `6f7889b9fb1a62a9577e685c1fcfa919` |
| JA4 | `t13d1717h2_5b57614c22b0_3cbfd9057e0d` | `t13d1717h2_5b57614c22b0_3cbfd9057e0d` |
| Akamai H2 | `6ea73faa8fc5aac76bded7bd238f6433` | `6ea73faa8fc5aac76bded7bd238f6433` |
| HTTP headers | Identical (except UA version) | Identical (except UA version) |

This means **something in Camoufox's C++ patches is being detected** at the JS/browser-behavior level.

**Test matrix (same machine, same IP, headless):**

| Site | Stock Firefox 146 (Playwright) | Camoufox 135 | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| hilton.com | 200 + Akamai challenge (5/5) | 403 flat reject (5/5) | Akamai won't even serve the challenge |
| nike.com | 200 OK | 200 OK | Less strict Akamai config |
| nordstrom.com | 200 OK | 200 OK | |
| dell.com | 200 OK | 200 OK | |
| lowes.com | 200 OK | 200 OK | |
| airbnb.com | 200 OK | 200 OK | |
| homedepot.com | 403 Blocked | 403 Blocked | Blocks all headless |

The hilton.com case is particularly telling: stock Firefox gets a 200 with a behavioral JS challenge (which a real browser can solve), while Camoufox gets a flat 403 rejection — Akamai flags it *before* any JS executes.

**Additional finding — viewport/screen dimension mismatch:**

Camoufox spoofs JS-reported dimensions but the actual Playwright viewport doesn't match:

```
Playwright viewport: {'width': 1280, 'height': 720}
JS window.innerWidth: 1920
JS screen.width: 1920 (or randomized value)
```

CSS media queries and page layout render at the real 1280px width (responsive/mobile layout), while JS APIs report 1920px (desktop). This mismatch is detectable by any script that compares CSS layout breakpoints against `window.innerWidth`. Setting `page.set_viewport_size()` to match doesn't fix the Akamai block, but it's an additional inconsistency worth noting.

**Configurations tested (all still blocked on hilton.com):**

- `exclude_addons=[DefaultAddons.UBO]` — no effect
- `os='linux'` — no effect
- `block_webrtc=True` — no effect
- `block_webgl=True` — no effect
- `headless='virtual'` (Xvfb) — no effect
- `config={'disableTheming': False}` — no effect
- `config={'memorysaver': False}` — no effect
- `enable_cache=True` — no effect
- `window=(1920, 1080)` + `page.set_viewport_size()` — no effect
- Manually setting consistent Linux navigator properties — no effect

No runtime configuration fixes the block. The detection appears to be in the compiled patches themselves.

**Suspected patches:**
Based on issue #450 (where `no-css-animations.patch` was identified as a detection vector for DataShield), one or more of these compiled patches may be detectable by Akamai:
- `no-css-animations.patch`
- `canvas-spoofing.patch`
- `font-list-spoofing.patch` (letter spacing randomization)
- `navigator-spoofing.patch`
- Other debloat/theming patches that alter default Firefox behavior

**Environment:**
- OS: Linux (Ubuntu, x86_64)
- Camoufox: v135.0.1-beta.24 (latest)
- Python camoufox package: latest from PyPI
- Playwright: 1.58.0
- Proxy: No
- Headless: True (also tested with `virtual`)

### To Reproduce

```python
# This gets blocked (403):
from camoufox.sync_api import Camoufox

with Camoufox(headless=True) as browser:
    page = browser.new_page()
    resp = page.goto("https://www.hilton.com", timeout=15000)
    print(resp.status)  # 403

# This works fine (200 + solvable challenge):
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

with sync_playwright() as p:
    browser = p.firefox.launch(headless=True)
    page = browser.new_page()
    resp = page.goto("https://www.hilton.com", timeout=15000)
    print(resp.status)  # 200
    browser.close()
```

### TLS fingerprint verification

Verified using `https://tls.browserleaks.com/json` — both browsers produce identical JA3, JA4, and Akamai HTTP/2 fingerprints, confirming the detection is at the application/JS layer, not the network layer.

title: Parallelization issue in context and page opening
body:
### Describe the bug:

Camoufox hangs and does weird things when using parallel coroutines in python with the `browser.new_context()` and `browser.new_page()` APIs. When invoking this calls within an asyncio.Lock(), the issue is no longer reproduced.

### Screenshots:

I only get a hanging coroutine and a timeout exception, nothing worthy to show.

### To Reproduce:

Given a python 3 script environment over camoufox 135.0.1-beta.24,
And creating a browser instance,
And spawning two parallel asyncio coroutines to interact with the same browser instance (using asnycio.gather),
When invoking `await browser.new_context()` or `await browser.new_page()` in the two parallel coroutines without serialization guard,
Then camoufox will only return either a single context or a single page instance, and lock the second coroutine.

After this,
When calling `await page.goto(self.url, wait_until="domcontentloaded")` on the returned page instance,
Then camoufox will never resolve this, and time out,
And the page content will always be empty on this page instance.

The expected behaviour should be that `new_context()` and `new_page()` are at least reentrant, even if not thread safe.

### Version:

135.0.1-beta.24
