Replace disable-remote-subframes.patch with webContentIsolationStrategy=0
body:
Closes #549
Related: #533, #150, #182

## Summary

Removes `disable-remote-subframes.patch` and switches `fission.webContentIsolationStrategy` from `1` to `0`. Fixes nested cross-origin iframe navigation while preserving the original goal: no out-of-process iframes.

## What was broken

Cross-origin iframes inside other iframes don't navigate — they exist in the DOM with correct `src` attributes but never load. Breaks any site that nests a captcha inside a wrapper iframe (Imperva/hCaptcha, Turnstile).

## Root cause

`disable-remote-subframes.patch` gates `SetRemoteSubframes()` behind `MaskConfig::GetBool("enableRemoteSubframes")`. Since that key is never set, `mUseRemoteSubframes` stays `false`. But `CreateDetached()` (line ~535) copies `mUseRemoteSubframes` directly from the parent — bypassing the setter. Every child context inherits `false`, cascading through all nesting levels. Combined with `fission.autostart=true`, nested cross-origin iframes silently fail.

## The fix

`webContentIsolationStrategy=0` (`IsolateNothing`) makes `ShouldIsolateSite()` return `false` for all content. Iframes stay same-process — identical to the old patch — but `mUseRemoteSubframes` stays `true` and propagates correctly through `CreateDetached()`.

## Why this aligns with existing intent

- **#150**: The original Turnstile issue. daijro's goal was "Disable OOPIFs without disabling COOP" — strategy=0 achieves exactly that.
- **#182**: daijro's [suggested fix](https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/issues/182#issuecomment-2666028244) was `{"fission.webContentIsolationStrategy": 0}` — the same change this PR makes permanent.
- **camoufox.cfg** already had strategy=0 as a commented-out alternative: `// Disable cross-process iframes, but not cross-process navigations.`
- **Commit 14270cd** (cross-process storage via Preferences API) removed `dom.ipc.processCount=1`, eliminating the original reason for same-process iframes — but the patch stayed.
- **Commit 43d273d** added MaskConfig fallback with the note: *"don't need to disable fission."*

## What's preserved

- `fission.autostart=true` — WAFs still see Fission enabled
- COOP handling — `ShouldCrossOriginIsolate()` is a separate code path, unaffected
- BFCache-in-parent, fingerprint spoofing — unaffected

## Detection risk

Strategy 0 vs 1 has no JS-observable difference — no DOM API, no `window` property, no timing side-channel. Playwright sets strategy=0 in its own `playwright.cfg`, but that's detected via profile prefs, not JS — and Camoufox controls its own prefs.

## Regression risk

- `disable_coop` becomes less critical but remains as an escape hatch
- `enableRemoteSubframes` config key removed — silently ignored if passed (consistent with unknown key handling)

## Test results

```
  PASS  A: Vanilla Firefox — flat page (baseline)
  PASS  B: Vanilla Firefox — nested iframe
  PASS  C: Camoufox — flat page
  PASS  D: Camoufox — nested iframe      (previously FAIL)
  PASS  E: Camoufox minimal — nested iframe (previously FAIL)
```

---

May also address [#307](https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/issues/307) (iframe JS context inaccessible) and [#283](https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/issues/283) (captcha checkbox/frame not found) — both symptoms of nested cross-origin iframes not loading.

title: Nested cross-origin iframes don't load — mUseRemoteSubframes=false cascades to all child contexts
body:
### The problem

Cross-origin iframes inside other iframes don't load. The inner iframes exist in the DOM with correct `src` attributes, but never navigate — zero network requests. This breaks any site that nests a captcha inside a wrapper iframe (Imperva/hCaptcha, Turnstile in some configurations).

Flat pages work fine — hCaptcha renders perfectly at the top level. It's specifically iframes-within-iframes that fail.

Built a minimal reproduction: an HTML page that nests hCaptcha inside a same-origin iframe. Vanilla Playwright Firefox: works. Camoufox (any config, even fully stripped down): fails.

### Root cause

`disable-remote-subframes.patch` (commit 8a1abfb) gates `BrowsingContext::SetRemoteSubframes()` behind `MaskConfig::GetBool("enableRemoteSubframes")`. Since that key is never set, `mUseRemoteSubframes` stays `false` in the top-level context.

The problem: there's a second write site the patch doesn't cover — `CreateDetached()` (line ~535):

```cpp
context->mUseRemoteSubframes = inherit->mUseRemoteSubframes;
```

This copies directly from the parent, bypassing the setter. Every child context inherits `false`, cascading through all nesting levels. Combined with `fission.autostart=true`, Firefox is in an inconsistent state — Fission is "on" but all contexts have remote subframes disabled — and nested cross-origin iframes silently fail.

### Proposed fix

The original patch was solving the right problem (#150 — Playwright can't click into OOPIFs). The goal was keeping iframes same-process while leaving COOP intact. `webContentIsolationStrategy=0` achieves that more cleanly — `ShouldIsolateSite()` returns `false` for all content, so iframes stay same-process. But `mUseRemoteSubframes` stays `true` and propagates normally through `CreateDetached()`, so nested navigation works.

Strategy 0 vs 1 has no JS-observable difference — no DOM API, no `window` property, no timing side-channel. The "WAFs can detect this!" comment in camoufox.cfg annotates `fission.autostart=true`, not the strategy value. COOP handling, BFCache-in-parent, and fingerprint spoofing are all unaffected.

I've got a build with this change that passes all tests. Happy to submit a PR.

Related: #533 (earlier report of the same symptom)

title: Allow disabling font spacing perturbation (seed=0 no-op, matching audio)
body:
Closes #547

## Summary

- Remove hardcoded `0x6D2B79F5u` fallback from font spacing perturbation
- Add `seed == 0` guard to skip perturbation (consistent with `AudioFingerprintManager`)
- Remove debug `printf` from the shaping path

## Description

### The inconsistency

Audio fingerprint perturbation has a clean off switch — `ApplyTransformation()` returns early when `seed == 0`. Font spacing doesn't: when no seed is set via `FontSpacingSeedManager`, the code falls back to a hardcoded constant (`0x6D2B79F5u`) and always applies perturbation.

This is a problem because the perturbation produces font/canvas hashes outside the real-device population. Fingerprint checkers with population databases (e.g. PixelScan) flag these as synthetic — "Masking detected". Being able to disable perturbation lets users choose plausibility over diversity when that tradeoff matters.

### The fix

Remove the hardcoded fallback and wrap the LCG + glyph offset loop in a `seed != 0` guard:

```cpp
uint32_t seed = FontSpacingSeedManager::GetSeed(pbid);

if (seed != 0) {
    // existing LCG + spacing application
}
```

When `GetSeed()` returns 0 (no seed set), the guard skips perturbation entirely. Same semantics as `AudioFingerprintManager::ApplyTransformation()`.

To disable from the Python API, set `fonts:spacing_seed` to 0 in the config/preset — same convention as `audio:seed` and `canvas:seed`.

Default behaviour is unchanged — `generate_context_fingerprint()` generates random non-zero seeds in `[1, 2^32-1]` as before, same as `audio:seed` and `canvas:seed`. This just makes it possible to opt out by passing 0, which font spacing was the only perturbation that didn't support.

### Side fix

Also removes the `printf("HarfBuzzShaper: ...")` debug statement that fires on every `ShapeText()` call (~4000 times per page load). This was instrumentation from development that shouldn't ship.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Regression risk

Low. The only behaviour change is:
1. **No seed explicitly set + no init script**: previously got perturbation via `0x6D2B79F5u` fallback, now gets vanilla metrics. This is the "bare Camoufox with no Python wrapper" case — unlikely to be anyone's production setup, and the new behaviour (no perturbation) is arguably more correct.
2. **Normal usage via Python API**: unchanged. Seeds are generated in range `[1, 2^32-1]` as before — perturbation on by default.
3. **Explicit seed=0**: new opt-out path that didn't exist before.

title: Font spacing perturbation has no off switch (unlike audio/canvas)
body:
Related: #76 — PixelScan reports 5 checks; this is the fix for the "Fingerprint: Masking detected" one specifically. The other four (Browser, Location, Proxy, Bot check) are unrelated to font spacing — see below.

## Problem

`AudioFingerprintManager::ApplyTransformation()` has a clean off switch — when `seed == 0`, it returns early and produces vanilla audio output. Font spacing perturbation doesn't have this: when no seed is set, `gfxHarfBuzzShaper.cpp` falls back to a hardcoded constant (`0x6D2B79F5u`) and always applies perturbation.

This means every Camoufox session produces font metrics and canvas text hashes that no real device has ever generated. Fingerprint checkers that maintain a population database (PixelScan's "Masking detected" verdict) can trivially flag this as synthetic.

| Perturbation | `seed == 0` behaviour | Hardcoded fallback | Can disable from Python? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Audio** | returns early, no-op | none | yes — set `audio:seed` to 0 |
| **Font spacing** | LCG still runs (0 → 12345) | `0x6D2B79F5u` when no seed set | no |
| **Canvas** | returns early, no-op | none | yes — set `canvas:seed` to 0 |

The audio and canvas paths let you opt out. Font spacing doesn't — inconsistent and makes A/B testing impossible from the Python API.

## Evidence

PixelScan runs 5 checks. With the font spacing fallback removed, the Fingerprint check flips from fail to pass:

| PixelScan check | Before fix | After fix | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Browser** | pass | pass | Firefox correctly identified |
| **Location** | pass | pass | Geoip/timezone cross-check |
| **Proxy** | fail (when proxied) | fail (when proxied) | IP reputation — unrelated |
| **Fingerprint** | **fail — "Masking detected"** | **pass** | Font spacing was the trigger |
| **Bot check** | pass | pass | Juggler protocol not flagged |

Tested across 6 Camoufox runs + 1 vanilla Firefox baseline. A custom build with the hardcoded fallback removed passes the Fingerprint check cleanly.

## Current C++ behaviour

```cpp
// gfxHarfBuzzShaper.cpp — ShapeText()
uint32_t seed = FontSpacingSeedManager::GetSeed(pbid);
bool seedFromManager = (seed != 0);
if (!seedFromManager) {
    seed = 0x6D2B79F5u; // always-on fallback
}
// LCG + spacing applied unconditionally
```

Compare with audio:

```cpp
// AudioFingerprintManager::ApplyTransformation()
if (seed == 0 || length == 0 || !data) {
    return;  // clean no-op
}
```

## Suggested fix

Remove the hardcoded fallback and guard the perturbation block, same as audio:

```cpp
uint32_t seed = FontSpacingSeedManager::GetSeed(pbid);

if (seed != 0) {
    // LCG + apply spacing (existing code, just wrapped in the guard)
}
```

When no seed is set, `GetSeed()` returns 0, the guard skips perturbation, and you get vanilla font metrics. To disable from the Python API, set `fonts:spacing_seed` to 0 in the config/preset — same convention as `audio:seed` and `canvas:seed`.

Happy to put up a PR if this looks reasonable.

title: Fix worker timezone leak when using geoip/proxy
body:
Closes #545

## Summary

Add `MaskConfig::GetString("timezone")` fallback to `TimezoneManager::GetTimezone()` so worker threads pick up the correct proxy timezone.

## Description

When `geoip=True`, the timezone is resolved from the proxy IP and stored in `CAMOU_CONFIG`. Playwright's `timezone_id` picks it up for the main thread. But `WorkerPrivate::GetOrCreateGlobalScope()` reads via `TimezoneManager::GetTimezone()` → `RoverfoxStorageManager`, which is empty — nothing has written to it via this path. Workers fall back to the host system timezone.

The fix adds a `MaskConfig` fallback to `TimezoneManager::GetTimezone()`: if storage is empty, read from `CAMOU_CONFIG` and store the result. Same pattern `AudioFingerprintManager::GetSeed()` already uses for `audio:seed`.

Also moved `SetTimezone`/`GetTimezone` from the header into `TimezoneManager.cpp` — `MaskConfig.hpp` can't be included from exported headers (they get copied to `obj-*/dist/include/` where the camoucfg include path isn't available).

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Testing

Verified with a US proxy on a UK host machine — worker timezone now matches main thread. Build-tester and web-tester results pending.

title: Worker threads leak real system timezone when proxied
body:
## Bug

When using a proxy in a different timezone to the host machine, worker threads report the real system timezone instead of the proxy timezone. Any fingerprint detector that checks `Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone` in both the main thread and a worker will spot the mismatch.

Invisible when proxy and host are in the same timezone — easy to miss in testing.

## Reproduction

```python
import asyncio
from camoufox.async_api import AsyncCamoufox

async def main():
    async with AsyncCamoufox(
        headless=True,
        proxy={"server": "http://PROXY:PORT", "username": "USER", "password": "PASS"},
        geoip=True,
    ) as browser:
        context = await browser.new_context()
        page = await context.new_page()

        main_tz = await page.evaluate(
            "Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone"
        )
        worker_tz = await page.evaluate("""() => new Promise(resolve => {
            const blob = new Blob(
                ['self.postMessage(Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone)'],
                {type: 'application/javascript'}
            );
            const w = new Worker(URL.createObjectURL(blob));
            w.onmessage = e => resolve(e.data);
        })""")

        print(f"Main:   {main_tz}")    # e.g. America/New_York (correct)
        print(f"Worker: {worker_tz}")  # e.g. Europe/London   (host system — wrong)

asyncio.run(main())
```

## Root cause

Three independent timezone mechanisms that don't fully talk to each other:

| Mechanism | Main thread | RoverfoxStorage | Workers |
|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| Playwright `timezone_id` / `docShell.overrideTimezone()` | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
| `window.setTimezone()` init script | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| `CAMOU_CONFIG` env var (`MaskConfig`) | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |

With `geoip=True`, the timezone ends up in `CAMOU_CONFIG` and Playwright sets it via `timezone_id`. Main thread is fine. But the worker hook in `WorkerPrivate::GetOrCreateGlobalScope()` reads from `RoverfoxStorageManager`, which is empty — nothing has populated it.

## Proposed fix

Add a `MaskConfig::GetString("timezone")` fallback to `TimezoneManager::GetTimezone()`. If storage is empty, read from `CAMOU_CONFIG` and store for future lookups. Same pattern `AudioFingerprintManager::GetSeed()` already uses for `audio:seed`.

Happy to put up a PR if this looks right to you.

title: Enable ccache for faster incremental builds
body:
## Summary

Add \`--with-ccache=ccache\` to \`assets/base.mozconfig\` and install instructions to CONTRIBUTING.md.

## Description

Safe no-op when ccache isn't installed — the build skips caching silently. When it is, incremental rebuilds drop from ~40 minutes to ~5 minutes after a single-file change, and to ~8 minutes after a full \`make setup\` re-extract.

That last one's the real win — \`make setup\` nukes all timestamps so the build system thinks everything changed. ccache sees the content hasn't changed and skips recompilation.

Tested on Apple M3 Max, 128 GB RAM. Binary output is identical with or without ccache.

- [x] Non-breaking change (no impact on fingerprinting or test results)
- [x] Documentation update

No test suite run needed — this only changes build tooling, not the browser binary.

title: Fix brotli/zstd decompression broken by Accept-Encoding override
body:
## Related Issue

Closes #542

## Description

When `headers.Accept-Encoding` is set via config (which browserforge does by default), brotli and zstd responses come back as garbled binary. gzip/deflate work fine.

**Root cause:** `SetAcceptEncodings` is called 3 times during init to populate 3 different member variables:

- `mHttpAcceptEncodings` — plain HTTP header
- `mHttpsAcceptEncodings` — HTTPS header
- `mDictionaryAcceptEncodings` — superset, used by `IsAcceptableEncoding()` to decide whether to install a decompressor

The current patch sets `mHttpsAcceptEncodings` and returns early on every call, so the other two are never populated. The outgoing header is fine (that uses `mHttpsAcceptEncodings`), but when the response comes back, `IsAcceptableEncoding("br", true)` checks `mDictionaryAcceptEncodings` — which is empty — and rejects it. gzip/deflate only survive because there's a hardcoded fallback for those two.

**Fix:** Instead of returning early, just swap out the input parameter and let the original branching logic do its thing. The config override still works exactly as intended — it just doesn't short-circuit the routing anymore.

- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Other

title: Brotli/zstd decompression broken when headers.Accept-Encoding is set via config
body:
When `headers.Accept-Encoding` is set via config (which browserforge does by default), brotli and zstd-compressed responses come back as garbled binary. gzip and deflate work fine.

## Symptoms

- Pages served with `Content-Encoding: br` render as raw compressed bytes
- Console error: "The byte stream was erroneous according to the character encoding that was declared"
- The outgoing `Accept-Encoding` header correctly includes `br` and `zstd`
- gzip/deflate responses decode fine

## Root cause

`SetAcceptEncodings` in `nsHttpHandler.cpp` is called three times during init, once per member variable:

- `mHttpAcceptEncodings` — plain HTTP header
- `mHttpsAcceptEncodings` — HTTPS header (used for the outgoing `Accept-Encoding`)
- `mDictionaryAcceptEncodings` — superset, used by `IsAcceptableEncoding()` to gate decompressor installation

The `network-patches.patch` override sets `mHttpsAcceptEncodings` and returns early on every call. The header goes out correctly, but `IsAcceptableEncoding("br", true)` checks `mDictionaryAcceptEncodings` — which is never populated — and returns false. No brotli decompressor is installed. gzip/deflate survive only because of a hardcoded fallback.

## Fix

Replace the input parameter instead of returning early, letting the original routing logic populate all three variables. One-line change in `network-patches.patch`. PR to follow.

## Affected versions

Any build where `headers.Accept-Encoding` is set via `CAMOU_CONFIG` or per-context config — i.e. effectively all normal usage via browserforge.

title: Worker threads leak real system timezone when using geoip/proxy
body:
## Problem

When timezone is set via `geoip=True` (or `timezone_id` context option), the main thread gets the correct proxy timezone but **worker threads fall back to the real system timezone**. Any fingerprint detector comparing `Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone` between the main thread and a worker can spot the discrepancy.

## Reproduction

Use a proxy in a different timezone than the host machine:

```python
import asyncio
from camoufox.async_api import AsyncCamoufox

async def main():
    async with AsyncCamoufox(
        headless=True,
        proxy={"server": "http://US_PROXY:PORT", "username": "USER", "password": "PASS"},
        geoip=True,
    ) as browser:
        context = await browser.new_context()
        page = await context.new_page()

        main_tz = await page.evaluate("Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone")
        worker_tz = await page.evaluate("""() => new Promise(resolve => {
            const blob = new Blob([
                'self.postMessage(Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone)'
            ], {type: 'application/javascript'});
            const w = new Worker(URL.createObjectURL(blob));
            w.onmessage = e => resolve(e.data);
        })""")

        print(f"Main:   {main_tz}")   # e.g. America/New_York (correct)
        print(f"Worker: {worker_tz}")  # e.g. Europe/London (system tz — wrong)

asyncio.run(main())
```

## Root cause

`TimezoneManager::GetTimezone()` only checks `RoverfoxStorageManager`. When timezone is set via Playwright's `timezone_id` (which goes through `docShell.overrideTimezone()`), nothing populates `RoverfoxStorageManager` — so the worker hook in `WorkerPrivate::GetOrCreateGlobalScope()` finds nothing and falls back to the system timezone.

The `window.setTimezone()` init script path works correctly because it calls `TimezoneManager::SetTimezone()` which stores in `RoverfoxStorageManager`. But the `timezone_id` / `CAMOU_CONFIG` path doesn't.

## Proposed fix

Add a `MaskConfig::GetString("timezone")` fallback to `TimezoneManager::GetTimezone()`, same pattern as `AudioFingerprintManager::GetSeed()` for `audio:seed`. When storage is empty, read from `CAMOU_CONFIG` and store for future lookups.

title: Unknown symbols fix for default/persistent context
body:
### This  #FR solves the issue with unknown symbols on the page.

1. If you are lauching Camoufox using `persistent_context=True` kwarg passed into `Camoufox` or `AsyncCamoufox` and getting the bug you should pass an additional kwarg named `extra_http_headers`:

Example:

```python

with Camoufox(
    extra_http_headers={"accept-encoding": "identity"}, 
    persistent_context=True, 
    user_data_dir='dir',
) as something:
    do_something()
```

2. Else if you are launching default camoufox and use something like `Camoufox().__enter__()` for example:
```python
browser = Camoufox().__enter__()  # this will give us the `Browser` object

# so we need to create a new context here
# and to fix the bug with unknown symbols
# we should pass this kwarg into a new created context
context = browser.new_context(extra_http_headers={"accept-encoding": "identity"})
```

https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/issues/535#issuecomment-4104798907

### Describe the bug:

Hey, I've been running into an issue where iframes don't navigate to their `src` — they just sit at `about:blank` forever, zero network requests for the URL.

**What I'm seeing:** I'm testing against a site behind Imperva which serves a challenge page inside a nested iframe structure (main page → Imperva iframe → hCaptcha iframe inside that). In Camoufox the first iframe never navigates. Vanilla Playwright Firefox on the same machine, same IP, same moment — works every time, 4 frames, hCaptcha renders fine.

**What I've found so far:** I traced it to `disable-remote-subframes.patch` — it gates `BrowsingContext::SetRemoteSubframes()` behind `MaskConfig::GetBool("enableRemoteSubframes")`, which is never set anywhere in the Python launch code. Setting `enableRemoteSubframes: true` in the config helps — the first iframe loads *sometimes* — but it's flaky. Vanilla Firefox is rock solid by comparison.

Even when the first iframe does load and I can see the challenge text, the nested hCaptcha iframe never renders. So there might be a second issue with how `enableRemoteSubframes` propagates to child browsing contexts (I noticed line 539 of BrowsingContext.cpp does direct assignment of `mUseRemoteSubframes` from parent, bypassing the patched setter).

- Is `enableRemoteSubframes` meant to be set by users, or should the patch default to allowing it?

        const ext = gl.getExtension('WEBGL_debug_renderer_info');
        return ext ? gl.getParameter(ext.UNMASKED_RENDERER_WEBGL) : null;
    }""")

async def main():
    async with AsyncCamoufox(headless=True) as browser:
        for i in range(3):
            ctx = await AsyncNewContext(browser, os="windows")
            page = await ctx.new_page()
            await page.goto("[https://example.com](https://example.com)", wait_until="domcontentloaded")
            renderer = await read_webgl(page)
            print(f"Context #{i+1} WebGL: {renderer}")
            
            await ctx.close()

asyncio.run(main())

title: Service Test and Contributing Guides
Fix: Execute mach clobber before git clean to prevent 'mach not found…
body:
When running `make clean` or the patch script in Docker builds, the following error occurs:

   ```
   cd camoufox-146.0.1-beta.25 && git clean -fdx && ./mach clobber
   Removing ./config
   Removing ./third_party
   ...
   /bin/sh: 1: ./mach: not found
   make: *** [Makefile:114: clean] Error 127
   ```

   **Root cause**: `git clean -fdx` deletes all untracked files including the `mach` file itself, so the subsequent `./mach clobber` command fails.

   ## Solution

   Reorder the commands to execute `./mach clobber` **before** `git clean -fdx`, ensuring mach is available when clobber runs.

title: navigator.platform, hardwareConcurrency, and oscpu config overrides silently ignored — browser leaks real values
body:
## Description

`navigator.platform`, `navigator.hardwareConcurrency`, and `navigator.oscpu` config values are correctly passed to the Camoufox binary via `CAMOU_CONFIG_*` env vars, but the browser ignores them and returns the real machine values instead. `navigator.userAgent` and other properties (screen dimensions, WebGL, etc.) are correctly applied.

This is the same class of bug as #89 (Playwright overriding custom screen width/height), but for navigator properties.

## Environment

- **camoufox-js**: 0.9.1
- **Camoufox binary**: 146.0.1-beta.25
- **OS**: macOS (Apple M1) — but the bug applies to any OS where you spoof a different platform
- **Node.js**: via ts-node / bun

## Reproduction

Minimal repro — pass explicit config values and check what the browser reports:

```typescript
import { Camoufox } from 'camoufox-js';

const browser = await Camoufox({
  headless: false,
  config: {
    'navigator.platform': 'Win32',
    'navigator.hardwareConcurrency': 8,
    'navigator.oscpu': 'Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64',
    'navigator.userAgent': 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64; rv:146.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/146.0',
    'navigator.appVersion': '5.0 (Windows)',
  },
  i_know_what_im_doing: true,
  debug: true,
});

const context = await browser.newContext();
const page = await context.newPage();
await page.goto('about:blank');

const result = await page.evaluate(() => ({
  platform: navigator.platform,
  hardwareConcurrency: navigator.hardwareConcurrency,
  oscpu: navigator.oscpu,
  userAgent: navigator.userAgent,
}));

console.log(result);
await browser.close();
```

## Expected behavior

```json
{
  "platform": "Win32",
  "hardwareConcurrency": 8,
  "oscpu": "Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64",
  "userAgent": "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64; rv:146.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/146.0"
}
```

## Actual behavior

```json
{
  "platform": "MacIntel",
  "hardwareConcurrency": 14,
  "oscpu": "Intel Mac OS X 10.15",
  "userAgent": "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64; rv:146.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/146.0"
}
```

`navigator.userAgent` is correctly spoofed, but `platform`, `hardwareConcurrency`, and `oscpu` all leak the real machine values.

## Debug output confirms config is correct

With `debug: true`, the config sent to the binary is:

```
'navigator.platform': 'Win32',
'navigator.hardwareConcurrency': 8,
'navigator.oscpu': 'Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64',
'navigator.userAgent': 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64; rv:146.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/146.0',
```

All properties are listed in `properties.json` with correct types (`str`, `uint`, `str`). The config is serialized and passed via `CAMOU_CONFIG_*` env vars. The binary receives it but does not apply these three properties.

## Also tested with fingerprint parameter

Same result when using `generateFingerprint()` and passing via the `fingerprint` parameter — the `fromBrowserforge()` conversion correctly maps `fingerprint.navigator.platform` → `navigator.platform` in the config, but the binary still ignores it.

## Impact

This creates a trivially detectable fingerprint mismatch. On a Linux VPS with a Windows fingerprint:

- `navigator.userAgent` → `Windows NT 10.0` ✅
- `navigator.platform` → `Linux x86_64` ❌ (should be `Win32`)
- `navigator.oscpu` → `Linux x86_64` ❌ (should be `Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64`)
- `navigator.hardwareConcurrency` → real VPS cores ❌ (should be fingerprint value)

Any basic bot detection can catch this:
```js
if (navigator.userAgent.includes('Windows') && navigator.platform !== 'Win32') { /* bot */ }
```

## Properties that DO work

- `navigator.userAgent` ✅
- `navigator.appVersion` ✅
- `navigator.doNotTrack` ✅
- `screen.width` / `screen.height` ✅
- `webGl:renderer` / `webGl:vendor` ✅
- `canvas:aaOffset` ✅

## Related issues

- #89 — Same class of bug (Playwright overriding custom screen width/height) — was fixed
- #416 — navigator.oscpu cannot be set to undefined
- #311, #388 — Detection issues that may be partially caused by this bug

title: fix: only include proxy key in launch options when proxy is not None
body:
When proxy is None, the original code still includes "proxy": None in the returned launch options dictionary. This causes an error downstream when the server expects a proxy object but receives null, e.g.:
"Error launching server: proxy: expected object, got null Failed to launch browser."

The fix conditionally adds the proxy key only when proxy is not None, preventing the null value from being passed to the browser launcher.

title: headless="virtual" creates Xvfb with 1x1 pixel screen, causing rendering issues
body:
### Describe the bug:

When using `headless="virtual"` mode on Linux, Camoufox starts an Xvfb virtual display with a screen resolution of **1x1 pixels**.
As a result, page content exists in the DOM but does **not render correctly in screenshots**. Screenshots appear mostly blank or dark, with elements positioned incorrectly.

This makes `headless="virtual"` effectively unusable for visual output (screenshots or rendering-dependent workflows) on Linux.

---

### To Reproduce:

```python
from camoufox.async_api import AsyncCamoufox
import asyncio

async def main():
    async with AsyncCamoufox(headless="virtual") as browser:
        page = await browser.new_page()
        await page.goto("https://iphey.com/")
        await asyncio.sleep(30)

        # Text exists in the DOM
        text = await page.evaluate("document.body.innerText.substring(0, 100)")
        print(text)  # Outputs: "Your digital identity looks Trustworthy..."

        # Screenshot is mostly blank
        await page.screenshot(path="screenshot.png", full_page=True)

asyncio.run(main())
```

Check the running Xvfb process:

```bash
ps aux | grep Xvfb
```

Observed output:

```text
/usr/bin/Xvfb :99 -screen 0 1x1x24 ...
```

**Root cause:**
In `camoufox/virtdisplay.py` (line 33), the virtual display screen size is hardcoded to `1x1x24`, which is too small for proper rendering.

---

### Version:

```
Camoufox 0.4.11
OS: Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS
Python: 3.12
```

title: Deterministic Hardware Fingerprinting (Seed Persistence) for Session Reuse
body:
## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

**The Problem:**
Currently, `persistent_context=True` successfully persists storage states (Cookies, LocalStorage), but it does **not** persist the randomization seeds used for hardware fingerprinting.

Every time the browser instance is restarted (even with the same `user_data_dir`), Camoufox regenerates:
1.  **Canvas/WebGL/Audio Noise Seeds:** Causing the "Fingerprint ID" / "VisitorID" to change completely.
2.  **Hardware Concurrency:** The CPU core count reported by `navigator.hardwareConcurrency` drifts randomly (e.g., 16 -> 12 -> 14).
3.  **GPU Renderer Strings:** Often switch between different mocked vendors.

**The Impact:**
For automation workflows requiring long-term session reuse, this behavior is problematic. Anti-fraud systems interpret this as "Session Hijacking" because the user identity (Cookies) remains the same, but the device characteristics (Hardware Fingerprint) abruptly change.

## Describe the solution you'd like

I request a mechanism to make the hardware fingerprint **deterministic** based on the profile data.

**Proposed Logic:**
1.  When a `user_data_dir` is initialized, generate the randomization seeds (Canvas/WebGL noise, Hardware Concurrency value, etc.) once.
2.  Save these seeds/configurations into a file within the `user_data_dir` (e.g., `fingerprint_config.json` or inside `user.js`).
3.  On subsequent launches pointing to this directory, **load these existing seeds** instead of generating new random ones.

This would ensure that a specific profile always "looks" like the exact same device, enabling true session persistence.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

1.  **Commercial Anti-detect Browsers + Playwright/Rebrowser:**
    * *Failure:* We attempted to automate popular commercial fingerprint browsers using Playwright and Rebrowser patches. However, the external CDP connection often triggers **Cloudflare** checks immediately. Camoufox's internal integration proves to be much stealthier against Cloudflare, which is why we prefer sticking with Camoufox if the persistence issue can be solved.
2.  **JS Injection (e.g., `page.add_init_script`):**
    * *Limitation:* This fails to cover **Web Workers**, which are commonly used by advanced fingerprinting libraries to detect inconsistencies.
3.  **Keeping the browser open indefinitely:**
    * *Limitation:* Not scalable for resource-constrained environments.

## Additional context

* **OS:** Linux / Windows
* **Use Case:** RPA with strict consistency requirements.

# Camoufox Detection Issue

## Website/Service Detecting Camoufox

[Discord.com](http://Discord.com) - specifically their hCaptcha implementation

## Detailed Description

When attempting to access Discord, I’m consistently running into hCaptcha validation issues. The captcha loads normally, but after completing it, I receive an “invalid-response” error every single time. This happens regardless of how carefully I solve the captcha.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Navigate to Discord login page
1. Enter valid credentials
1. hCaptcha challenge appears
1. Complete the captcha challenge
1. Receive “invalid-response” error
1. Loop continues indefinitely - unable to proceed

- Using `AsyncCamoufox()` initialization
- proxy being used
- Clean setup with default parameters

The hCaptcha itself renders and functions normally - I can interact with the challenge. However, the response token appears to be rejected on the backend, suggesting Discord’s hCaptcha implementation may be detecting something about the browser fingerprint that flags it as automated/suspicious.

The fact that it works fine in a regular browser on the same IP confirms this isn’t an IP reputation issue, but rather something specific to how Camoufox is being fingerprinted by hCaptcha’s detection system.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

# Camoufox browser window remains visible in WSL even when `headless` is set to `virtual`

## Description
When `headless` is set to `"virtual"`, the Camoufox browser window still appears on the screen in WSL2 on Windows 11. The goal is for the browser to remain fully invisible. Setting `headless=False` hides the window, but triggers Captchas from systems like Datadome, so that’s not a viable solution.

I have verified that `Xvfb` is installed on the WSL VM and have followed the instructions from the [headless Linux docs](https://camoufox.com/python/virtual-display/).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Use Windows 11 and install WSL2.  
2. Follow Camoufox installation instructions for Linux ([docs](https://camoufox.com/python/installation/)).  
3. Launch Camoufox programmatically via a FastAPI server while setting `headless="virtual"`.  
4. Observe that the browser window still appears.

## Code Snippet
```python
async def scrape_sites(urls: list[str]) -> list[ScrapedSites]:
    async with AsyncCamoufox(os="linux",
                             webgl_config=("Intel", "Intel(R) HD Graphics, or similar"),
                             humanize=True,
                             headless="virtual",
                             geoip=True,
                             enable_cache=True
                             ) as browser:
        try:
            results = await asyncio.gather(
                *[scrape_site(browser, url) for url in urls],
                return_exceptions=True
            )
                
            final_results = []

            for i, result in enumerate(results):
                
                if isinstance(result, Exception):
                    print(f"Failed to scrape {urls[i]}: {result}")

                final_results.append(result)
                
            return final_results
        finally:
            try:
                await browser.close()
            except Exception:
                pass
```
## Version
```
Pip package: v0.4.11
Camoufox: v135.0.1-beta.24
```

## Notes
- Using FastAPI to launch the browser might be irrelevant, but included for context.  
- Behavior occurs despite following all `Xvfb`/headless setup instructions.

title: Fix launch_server, to be able to use persistent_context and user_data_dir
body:
## Issue #253 

When attempting to use `persistent_context` and `user_data_dir` parameters in `launch_server()`:

```python
launch_server(
    # ...
    persistent_context=True,
    user_data_dir='my-user-data-dir'
    # ...
)
```

These parameters are completely ignored - they are not read, parsed, or taken into account by the implementation.

## Solution

According to [playwright-core/src/browserServerImpl.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/main/packages/playwright-core/src/browserServerImpl.ts), the underlying implementation supports passing `_userDataDir` for persistent contexts.

This PR adds support for these parameters in `launch_server()` to enable persistent context functionality when launching browser servers.

title: `async` function not awaited in main world execution mode
body:
When evaluating an asynchronous function in the main world execution mode, the return value is always `{ }`.

Example:

```python
from camoufox.sync_api import Camoufox

with Camoufox(
    main_world_eval=True
) as camoufox:
    page = camoufox.new_page()
    result = page.evaluate("""mw:async () => ({"test": "value"})""")
    print(result)
```

Prints

```
{ }
```

After removing the `mw:` label, the script prints `{'test': 'value'}` as expected. Making the function sync (removing the `async` keyword while keeping `mw:`) will also run the function and print `{'test': 'value'}`.

title: Expand support to account for all properties of the fingerprint parameter
body:
### Describe the feature:
When passing the fingerprint parameter, camoufox will only support a subset of its attributes, which causes rotation of fingerprints even if its the same exact fingerprint passed on, effectively making it a useless parameter.

I am using Camoufox inside an API (aiohttp api, inside docker, 2 instances, each with 4 GB of memory). After running for a few days, the API fails. During debugging, I found that **memory usage increases** to 97–99%. **Here’s a simplified version of my code:** ``` try: async with AsyncCamoufox( locale=["en-US"], os="linux", block_webrtc=True, block_webgl=False, window=(1280, 720), headless="virtual", ) as browser: page = await browser.new_page() inter_url = f"https://www.example/interception" url = f"https://www.example" # intercepting an api url async with page.expect_response( lambda response: inter_url in response.url and response.status == 200, timeout=90000 ) as response_info: await page.goto(url, wait_until="load", timeout=90000) response = await response_info.value try: data = json.loads(await response.text()) await page.close() await browser.close() except Exception as error: logger.warning(f"Error occurred while fetching data: {error}") await page.close() await browser.close() except Exception as error: logger.error(f"Error occurred in browser: {error}") # Browser is not closing here , because if an exception happens the camoufox context will close it ``` **To investigate, I added logging to track processes and memory usage inside the API:** ````python def debug_processes(uid): for proc in psutil.process_iter(['pid', 'name', 'memory_info', 'cmdline']): try: logger.info( f"{GREEN}PID: {proc.info['pid']} | Name: {proc.info['name']} | " f"Memory: {proc.info['memory_info'].rss / 1024 ** 2:.2f} MB | " f"Cmd: {' '.join(proc.info['cmdline'])} | uid: {uid}{RESET}" ) except (psutil.NoSuchProcess, psutil.AccessDenied): continue ```` Whenever the **issue occurs**, I see hundreds of _**playwright/driver/node**_ processes running inside the API. title: Fix launch server breaking when no proxy option is passed.
body:
## Problem
  When launching Camoufox server without a proxy, the following error occurs:
  Error launching server: proxy: expected object, got null

  ## Root Cause
  The `launch_options()` function always includes `"proxy": proxy` in the returned dictionary, even when `proxy=None`. When serialized to JSON and      
  passed to Playwright's `launchServer()`, this becomes `"proxy": null`, which Playwright rejects.

  ## Solution
  Only include the proxy key in the returned options when `proxy` is not None. This matches Playwright's expectation that the proxy parameter
  should either be a valid object or completely absent.

  ## Changes
  - Modified the return statement in `launch_options()` to conditionally include proxy
  - Added conditional logic to exclude None proxy values
  - No breaking changes - existing code continues to work

title: Data Synchronization Across Devices with Continued Canvas CPU Fingerprint Protection
body:
I am a user of Camoufox and appreciate its robust privacy features, particularly the advanced spoofing of CPU Canvas fingerprints through manipulation of anti-aliasing logic (as discussed in [Discussion #41](https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/discussions/41)). However, I would like to propose adding a data synchronization feature to allow users to sync browser data (e.g., bookmarks, history, preferences, or tabs) across multiple devices using a single account, while ensuring that the existing Canvas fingerprint protection remains intact.
Proposed Feature

Data Synchronization:
Enable users to create or link a Camoufox account to sync browser data across devices (e.g., laptops, desktops, or mobile devices).
Data to sync could include bookmarks, browsing history, saved passwords, open tabs, and user preferences.
Synchronization should prioritize user privacy, possibly using end-to-end encryption to prevent data exposure, aligning with Camoufox's privacy-focused mission.


Canvas CPU Fingerprint Protection:
Ensure that the synchronization feature does not compromise the existing Canvas fingerprint spoofing mechanism (e.g., randomization of Skia’s anti-aliasing logic, as mentioned in Discussion #41).
The synced data should not include any identifiable fingerprinting information that could link devices or sessions, maintaining the effectiveness of Canvas anti-fingerprinting.
If possible, allow the Canvas fingerprint to remain consistent within a session across synced devices but randomized between sessions, as currently implemented.



Use Case

Scenario: A user works on a laptop and a desktop, both running Camoufox. They want to access their bookmarks and open tabs seamlessly across devices without manually exporting/importing data.
Privacy Requirement: The user expects Camoufox to maintain its strong anti-fingerprinting capabilities, ensuring that Canvas fingerprints remain spoofed and untraceable, even with data syncing enabled.
Example: Similar to Firefox Sync, but tailored to Camoufox’s privacy model, ensuring no data is stored on third-party servers unless encrypted.

Additional Considerations

Security: Use end-to-end encryption for synced data to prevent interception or tracking by third parties.
Performance: Ensure the sync feature does not introduce performance overhead or affect the rendering pipeline (e.g., Skia’s anti-aliasing logic).
Optional Toggle: Allow users to enable/disable synchronization in settings, preserving the lightweight nature of Camoufox for those who don’t need syncing.
Compatibility: Ensure the feature works across all supported platforms (Windows, macOS, Linux, and potentially mobile if Camoufox expands).

Related References

[Discussion #41: Graphical Canvas fingerprinting](https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/discussions/41) for details on Canvas fingerprint spoofing.
Camoufox’s closed-source patch for Skia’s anti-aliasing logic (mentioned on [camoufox.com](https://camoufox.com/)).
Firefox Sync as a potential model for privacy-respecting synchronization.

Questions for Maintainers

Is there any plan to implement data synchronization in Camoufox?
How feasible is it to integrate syncing while preserving the Canvas CPU fingerprint spoofing mechanism?
Are there technical or privacy-related challenges that need to be addressed to make this feature viable?

Thank you for considering this feature request! I look forward to hearing your thoughts or any updates on this topic.

title: fix: return correct country from geoip database
body:
Currently, `geoip2.model.City.registered_country` is used for determining locale. However, for the proxy I use, this leads to locale value being `crs-SC` (Seselwa Creole French), which is completely wrong. Every other value from geoip is fine, including `country`.
From [geoip2 docs](https://geoip2.readthedocs.io/en/latest/#geoip2.models.City.registered_country): 
> `registered_country`: The registered country object for the requested IP address. This record represents the country where the ISP has registered a given IP block in and may differ from the user’s country.

> `country`: Country object for the requested IP address. This record represents the country where MaxMind believes the IP is located.

I think `country` should be used in this case.

  - Enable performance timing fuzzing

  - Humanize scroll behavior

title: Camoufox freezes when asynchronously loading multiple pages
body:
### Describe the bug:

Opening multiple pages concurrently makes Camoufox seemingly freeze. Likely happening somewhere in the browser binary, as we're getting the same issue with `camoufox-js` (originally reported by @vastblast over at https://github.com/apify/camoufox-js/issues/19).

Replacing Camoufox with vanilla Playwright fixes this issue (the code runs and finishes).

### To Reproduce:

```python
from camoufox.async_api import AsyncCamoufox
import asyncio

async def open_page(browser, i: int):
    page = await browser.new_page()
    await page.goto('https://example.com')
    title = await page.title()
    print(f"{i} Loaded page with title: {title}")
    await page.close()

async def main():
    async with AsyncCamoufox(headless=True) as browser:
        await asyncio.gather(
            open_page(browser, 1),
            open_page(browser, 2),
            open_page(browser, 3)
        )

asyncio.run(main())
```

This code will only produce:

```text
3 Loaded page with title: Example Domain
```

and will hang indefinitely.

title: page.wait_for_load_state("networkidle") resolves immediately
body:
I found a discrepancy between Playwright and Camoufox API (using the async variant).

When you initiate an AJAX call, which takes some time, for example by clicking on a button. 
If you then call  `await page.wait_for_load_state("networkidle") ` it works differently in Playwright and in Camoufox:

Playwright - function resolves after the AJAX (and other calls) finishes - the default 500ms network idle.
Camoufox - It resolves immediately, taking into account only initial page load. After it resolves once, its always idle. 

Or maybe, is this intentional for Camoufox?

Have a nice day

title: Better humanization
body:
Some ideas in no particular order:

Human like scrolling behavior when scrolling elements into view. Cursor points on the element it wants to scroll and scrolling is done via the mouse wheel, with some uncertainty (go down, go up, go down) stutter etc.

Move the mouse to random points sometimes, although now the mouse trajectory seems human like if it always moves from one action thing to another action thing it is suspicious. It needs a little ADHD.

Humans will also just park their cursor for a bit on a random part of the page.

Also when entering the "desired" element to click on, just wait a bit before clicking, maybe even go back outside the element before re-entering and then click.

Add a randomized delay between actions, e.g. wait between 1-4 seconds between filling form fields. We could even define what an action is and then make sure that we don't do more than x actions a minute. Do some bogus actions in between maybe.

For typing, add random delays between characters. Maybe even a more complex algo which takes the keyboard layout into account. Make some mistakes while typing, but correct them.

Actions like .focus should be done with a humanized mouse cursor. Same for selecting the value of a select element. This also applies to other things like there should always be a click before fill or type. (Or alternatively simultate the tab key to switch between fields sometimes)

Add tiny random delays between multiple clicks on the same element e.g. double click.

Occasional small mouse movement while "typing".

I can help with some of the low hanging fruit, I just would like some feedback on my ideas first. Did I accidentally request anything that's already implemented?

Basically what I want from humanize is to set it to true and then just write the most straight forward playwright code to achieve the goal, but when running it looks like a human did it. I don't want to think about clicks, delays, typing etc.

I would like to add two new parameters to the browser config `min_action_delay` and `max_action_delay`.

title: Fix cleanup on exception in sync_api __enter__
body: If an exception is raised in the synchronous api during the setup, super().__enter__ has been called but super().__exit__ will not get called, leading to asyncio runloop exceptions further down the line if one tries to create a new context. This commit catches the exception in order to clean up the super().__exit__ calls before reraising.

title: Fix unbound exception ip function
body:
Variables assigned in `as` blocks are garbage collected at the end of the block. Hence even if we define `exception = None` the `exception` variable gets cleaned in the `as exception` block. And on the `raise InvalidIP` line we get an `UnboundLocalError` instead of an `InvalidIP` error with the exception information.

You can easily reproduce with something like:
```py
def invalid() -> None:
    exception = None
    try:
        raise ValueError("test")
    except ValueError as exception:
        pass
    raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to get IP address: {exception}")  # UnboundLocalError


invalid()  # UnboundLocalError
```

title: Slow startup and page loading
body:
I've noticed compared to default playwright firefox, this solution is extremely slow.
I have found that the slowest part is reading camoufox fingerprint env variable each time property is "patched". Simple fix is to cache it after first read/validate/parse loop. After recompiling browser with this fix, it now launches in under 2 seconds, similar to default playwright firefox. Also going to url works at least 4x faster too. 

My question is what is the purpose of multiple ENV with camoufox config? Is the idea to leave the browser running ant patch it during runtime? If not I would recommend reading ENV once and caching the parsed fingerprint. With these fixes browser launch median time in my benchmark is 1.5s, so it is not a big cost to restart each time instead of patching it during runtime.

title: Reusing Browser Sessions for Debugging with Persistent Browser Instance
body:
### Describe the feature:

Reusing Browser Sessions for Debugging with Persistent Browser Instance

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

### Issue Title: Feature Request: Reusing Browser Sessions for Debugging with Persistent Browser Instance

**Describe the bug**

I am trying to set up a persistent browser instance using a custom server (based on Camoufox, code provided below) and connect to it with Playwright for automated tasks.  My goal is to be able to reuse the browser session for debugging purposes, similar to how `--browser-reuse-context` works for local Playwright launches, but in a remote/connected browser scenario.

**Code Snippets**

Here is the code I use to launch the browser server (using `camoufox.server`):

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3

import os
import sys
import time
import signal
import traceback
from camoufox.server import launch_server

server = None

def signal_handler(sig, frame):
    """处理 SIGINT 信号 (Ctrl+C)"""
    print("\n正在关闭服务器...")
    # 简单地退出，不抛出异常
    sys.exit(0)

def main():
    global server
    print("启动 Camoufox 服务器...")

    # 注册信号处理程序
    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, signal_handler)

    try:
        # 使用你提供的参数配置
        launch_server(
            headless=False,  # 设置为 True 可以隐藏浏览器窗口
            geoip=True,
            proxy={
                'server': '127.0.0.1:8000',
                'username': 'proxy',
                'password': 'lmzsV0d'
            },
            # Camoufox 特定配置
            humanize=True,
            os='windows',
            webgl_config=("Google Inc. (NVIDIA)", "ANGLE (NVIDIA, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 980 Direct3D11 vs_5_0 ps_5_0), or similar"),
            # WebSocket 服务器配置
            port=1234,
            ws_path='browser'
        )
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"发生错误: {e}")
        print(traceback.format_exc())
        return 1

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

connect code.
```python

from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright
def connect_browser():
    p = sync_playwright().start()
    # 使用 firefox 实例的 server 属性连接
    browser = p.firefox.connect(
        'ws://localhost:1234/browser'
    )
    return p, browser

def main():
    playwright, browser = connect_browser()
    page = browser.new_page()
    page.goto("[https://www.google.com](https://www.google.com)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

Describe Expected Behavior

I would like to be able to connect to the same browser session across multiple script executions for debugging.  Ideally, when I run my Playwright script multiple times, it would reuse the existing browser instance launched by the server, preserving the browser state (cookies, local storage, etc.) and allowing me to inspect the browser in real-time for debugging.

Current Behavior

Currently, each time I run the Playwright script, it connects to the server and seems to create a new browser session or context.  The browser launched by the server persists, but the Playwright connection does not seem to reuse the existing session for debugging purposes in subsequent script runs.

Steps to reproduce

Run the server code to launch the persistent browser instance.
Run the Playwright connection code multiple times.
Observe that each script execution seems to start from a fresh browser state, rather than reusing the existing one for debugging.
Possible Solutions or Feature Requests

Is there a way to achieve browser session reuse for debugging in this connected browser scenario?  Perhaps there are specific connection parameters, headers, or Playwright API methods I am missing?

It would be extremely helpful if Playwright could provide a mechanism to reliably connect to and reuse existing browser sessions launched by external servers for debugging, similar to the --browser-reuse-context flag for local launches.  This would greatly improve the debugging experience when working with persistent or remote browser instances.

Any guidance or suggestions on how to achieve this, or if this could be considered as a feature request, would be greatly appreciated.

Thank you!

from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

def camoufox_screenshot():
    start_time = time.time()
    
    with Camoufox(

title: Deadlock when not excluding uBlockOrigin addon
body:
### Describe the bug:

When running multiple asyncio tasks for scraping without excluding the uBlockOrigin addon, a deadlock situation occurs during the `page.goto`. However, when the uBlockOrigin addon is excluded, the deadlock does not happen.

Info: I'm using one browser and multiple browser context.

### To Reproduce:

Here is a simple script to reproduce:
```python
import asyncio
import logging

from camoufox.addons import DefaultAddons
from camoufox.async_api import AsyncCamoufox
from playwright.async_api import Browser
from playwright.async_api import TimeoutError as PlaywrightTimeoutError

SCRAPING_DURATION = 1  # In minutes
NB_TASKS = 5
DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = 10
HTTP_OK = 200

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class ScrapingReport:
    def __init__(self):
        self.nb_scrapes = 0
        self.nb_success = 0
        self.nb_failures = 0

        self.lock = asyncio.Lock()

    def log(self):
        logger.info(f"Scrapes: {self.nb_scrapes}, Success: {self.nb_success}, Failures: {self.nb_failures}")

    async def increment_scrapes(self):
        async with self.lock:
            self.nb_scrapes += 1

    async def increment_success(self):
        async with self.lock:
            self.nb_success += 1

    async def increment_failures(self):
        async with self.lock:
            self.nb_failures += 1


scraping_report = ScrapingReport()


async def scrape(browser: Browser):
    ctx = await browser.new_context()
    page = await ctx.new_page()

    try:
        response = await page.goto("http://localhost:8003/hello.html", timeout=DEFAULT_TIMEOUT)
    except PlaywrightTimeoutError:
        response = None

    await scraping_report.increment_scrapes()
    if response and response.status == HTTP_OK:
        await scraping_report.increment_success()
    else:
        await scraping_report.increment_failures()

    await page.close()
    await ctx.close()


async def scrape_for_duration(browser: Browser, duration_minutes: int):
    start_time = asyncio.get_event_loop().time()
    while (asyncio.get_event_loop().time() - start_time) < duration_minutes * 60:
        await scrape(browser)

async def main():
    camoufox = AsyncCamoufox(
        headless=False,
        # exclude_addons=[DefaultAddons.UBO],
    )

    async with camoufox as browser:
        # Run NB_TASKS concurrent scrapes for SCRAPING_DURATION
        tasks = [asyncio.create_task(scrape_for_duration(browser, SCRAPING_DURATION)) for _ in range(NB_TASKS)]
        await asyncio.wait(tasks)
    
    scraping_report.log()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

Where `http://localhost:8003/hello.html` is a simple hello world html served locally:

`python -m http.server 8003 --bind 0.0.0.0`

You may notice that Camoufox hangs for no apparent reason at times.

### Result:

- With uBlockOrigin:
```
python main2.py
INFO:__main__:Scrapes: 65, Success: 55, Failures: 10
```
- Without uBlockOrigin:
```
python main2.py
INFO:__main__:Scrapes: 235, Success: 235, Failures: 0
```

### Environment and Version:
- OS: macOS (M1)
- Python: 3.12
- Camoufox:
```
Pip package:	v0.4.11
Camoufox:	v135.0-beta.21 (Up to date!)
```

title: Python Remote Server Graceful Shutdown
body:
### Describe the bug:

When using the python interface to launch a remote server, for example using the example script at: https://camoufox.com/python/remote-server/, everything run's fine, but calling browser.Close() and/or playwright.Stop() does not stop the server. This is most likely the preferred behavior but the real problem lies with the python launch_server, there is no way to gracefully stop the server, thus cleanup of temporary files never happens.

For example, run a server, do some work, close and kill the server, repeat, this quickly consumes the entire available disk space because there is no way to gracefully close the server so the directories below never get deleted

```
/tmp/playwright-artifacts-*
/tmp/playwright_firefoxdev_profile-*
```

### Screenshots:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4574c0a7-1262-419f-b57b-bb28640ed0ef)

### To Reproduce:

Run the example script: https://camoufox.com/python/remote-server/, close the the browser/context/playwright, and the temporary directories above are never deleted.

`Camoufox:       v133.0-beta.19 (Latest supported: v134.0.2-beta.20)`

title: Revisit camoufox.cfg
body:
Hi @daijro , I have been researching for some time the settings you are using in [camoufox.cfg](https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/blob/main/settings/camoufox.cfg) and comparing it with the one used in playwright's [file](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/main/browser_patches/firefox/preferences/playwright.cfg#L37).

While I understand how most of the settings improve the stealth and the performance of Camoufox, some seem not logical to have. It may be set in Camoufox's early versions and you didn't have a chance to revisit it. I wanted to make a PR but thought to create an issue to discuss these options and think out loud.

1. `dom.event.clipboardevents.enabled = false`
Websites can check if clipboard events are turned off by playing around with the `navigator.clipboard` for example, which will hurt Camoufox's stealth. I think turning it on will be better.

2. `dom.ipc.processCount = 1`
I can't figure out why you did this, you didn't explain it in the comments like what you did with other settings. I know this eliminates process isolation, but it's causing performance bottlenecks (especially with multiple tabs) as well as increasing crash risks. Can't we set the value of this to 4 for example? I don't know if this can be passed [as config as here or not.](https://camoufox.com/python/config/)

3. `privacy.resistFingerprinting = false`
Disabling Firefox’s anti-fingerprinting feature makes the browser more unique and detectable. Metrics like screen resolution, timezone, and fonts become easier to track. You have written a comment saying 'This will actually hurt fingerprinting.' next to it, is there still a reason to leave this disabled?

There are other settings I'm not sure about if I'm correct or not but these are more important, I'm looking forward to your answer. I love Camoufox and the work you are doing and I'm just trying to help improve it the way I know the best.

I think performance should take priority over memory usage like in Playwright. Being stealthy and fast is better than being stealthy and slow, you can add, for example, a page on the website for what settings to turn off to save memory for people who prioritize that but I don't think it's ideal to make it slow browsing is the default behavior as Camoufox is significantly slower than Playwright.

title: Can't click interactive turnstile with Camoufox like patchright
body:
Hey mate, there is this new script that can click interactive turnstile captcha: https://github.com/Xewdy444/CF-Clearance-Scraper
I tested it on https://sergiodemo.com/security/challenge/legacy-challenge and it worked
The main version uses Patchright and there's another one with nodriver. Both can only bypass it in headed mode.

The thing is I tried to make a version that does this with Camoufox but it doesn't work, here's my research results:
1. Because the script depends on clicking on specific [hard-coded dimensions](https://github.com/Xewdy444/CF-Clearance-Scraper/blob/playwright/main.py#L197) on the page, it needs the browser to show with the default viewport/window size of Playwright's Chrome.
I searched it and found it's OS dependent so for my MacOS it's `{'width': 1280, 'height': 720}`. I used the attribute `window=(width, height)` of Camoufox but the window keeps opening in different sizes every time.
So I used the `screen` argument as well like this `screen=Screen(max_width=width, min_width=width, max_height=height, min_height=height)` and the window now opens in the same size but still something doesn't look right.
So I added another test: 
`print(self.page.viewport_size)`
`print(self.page.evaluate("({ width: window.innerWidth, height: window.innerHeight })"))`
and it turns out the height on the second print is always wrong!
2. The page takes more time to load than Patchright and about double the time for the captcha spinner to disappear, something seems really off with the page on Camoufox. I think browserforge fingerprints are missing something, I was using it on [Scrapling](https://github.com/D4Vinci/Scrapling) to inject headers to raw playwright and I had many issues with normal websites not loading that don't have protections and recaptcha not loading. In the end, it turns out the format used in browserforge headers is very old and different than the one used in Chrome now so just disabling it made all those websites load correctly.

With Camoufox the function called [solve_challenge](https://github.com/Xewdy444/CF-Clearance-Scraper/blob/playwright/main.py#L172) doesn't work at all no matter how I optimize it for Camoufox, it doesn't detect any of the elements.

I guess all this problem revolves around Camoufox taking too much control over what's happening without too many options for the user to control the behavior. I don't know.

Last month I made a script to click the turnstile interactive captcha the same way but depending on OpenCV for the dimensions and Camoufox as a browser but I had a big issue with the mouse click not registering and I think this happens here too. Maybe Camoufox handles nested iframes very differently than Patchright?

Enable **Camoufox** to support **noDriver** mode. body: ### Describe the bug: When Camoufox is idle, it uses almost twice as much CPU as Playwright Firefox in headed mode. I noticed this even on a static page with no active tasks. It seems like the issue is related to the GUI constantly redrawing itself. ### How I observed it: The issue really showed its true colors when I decided to debug it with a VNC connection, though VNC is not mandatory. Playwright startup script: ```sh playwright open -b firefox https://google.com ``` Camoufox 'start.py': ```python from camoufox.sync_api import Camoufox from browserforge.fingerprints import Screen with Camoufox( geoip=True, humanize=True, headless=False, window=(1024, 768), screen=Screen(max_width=1024,min_width=1024, max_height=768,min_height=768), firefox_user_prefs={ "layout.css.always_underline_links": False }, config={'showcursor': False}, ) as camoufox: page = camoufox.new_page() page.wait_for_timeout(1000) page.goto('https://google.com') page.wait_for_timeout(999999999) ``` 1. Started a VNC server 2. Ran the application in headed mode (used virtual display from the VNC server) 3. Connected a VNC client. 4. In browser searched for "beer" (static page: no animations, no videos). 5. Waited and watched the CPU usage with the VNC connected. 6. Disconnected the VNC client and checked CPU usage again. This approach worked, and it pointed to something happening with how the GUI interacts with VNC. **Playwright Firefox:** Idle (no VNC client): ~14% vCPU **Camoufox:** Idle (no VNC client): ~25% vCPU Now let's look at the traffic when VNC client is connected (out traffic means GUI is updated): **Playwright Firefox:** **Camoufox:** **What is sent to VNC client?** I checked what data Camoufox was sending to the VNC client. Turns out, it keeps redrawing the custom theme GUI header over and over, which explains the extra network traffic: ### Version: ``` Pip package: v0.4.6 Camoufox: v133.0-beta.18 (Up to date!) ```

title: Ensure WebGL support by adjusting Xvfb configuration
body:
Firefox requires a display to enable WebGL support, see https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/issues/114#issuecomment-2524720064.

Camoufox already provides a virtual display by spawning Xvfb with a screen resolution of 1x1 and an 8-bit color depth.

However, 8-bit color depth is insufficient to activate WebGL in Firefox. After testing various Xvfb configurations, it was determined that the minimum required settings are:

- 24-bit color depth
- GLX extension enabled

Update ensures that WebGL is available when running Firefox in the `headless="virtual"` mode.

**Changes Made:**

Updated Xvfb configuration to use 24-bit color depth.
Explicitly enabled the GLX extension to support OpenGL rendering.

**Manual testing script:**

```python
from camoufox.sync_api import Camoufox

with Camoufox(headless="virtual") as camoufox:
    page = camoufox.new_page()
    webgl_info = page.evaluate(
        """
        (()=>{
            try {
                const canvas = document.createElement('canvas');
                const webgl = canvas.getContext('webgl') || canvas.getContext('experimental-webgl');
                const info = webgl.getExtension('WEBGL_debug_renderer_info');
                const [vendor, renderer] = [webgl.getParameter(info.UNMASKED_VENDOR_WEBGL), webgl.getParameter(info.UNMASKED_RENDERER_WEBGL)]
                return `Vendor: ${vendor}\\nRenderer: ${renderer}`
            } catch (e) {
                return `No WebGL: ${e.message}`
            }
        })()
        """
    )
    print(webgl_info)
```

**Example of positive output:**

```console
Starting virtual display: /usr/bin/Xvfb :99 -screen 0 1x1x24 -ac -nolisten tcp -extension RENDER +extension GLX -extension COMPOSITE -extension XVideo -extension XVideo-MotionCompensation -extension XINERAMA -shmem -fp built-ins -nocursor -br
Vendor: Google Inc. (NVIDIA)
Renderer: ANGLE (NVIDIA, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 980 Direct3D11 vs_5_0 ps_5_0), or similar
```

title: Option to use exact user-specified fonts without loading from fonts.json
body:
### Describe the feature:

Is there a way to use the exact list of fonts entered by the user in the "fonts" key-value pair?

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Hello,

First of all, thank you for developing such an excellent library.

I am experiencing some difficulties with the [logic that applies fonts](https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/blob/99801bd139d99cff8159ef0ecad81876552d6da8/pythonlib/camoufox/utils.py#L174-L185).
According to the code, it appears that when generating the browser by specifying the "fonts" key value, the fonts are combined with the JSON values corresponding to the "os" value, which is determined before the font-related logic (maybe from [get_target_os](https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/blob/99801bd139d99cff8159ef0ecad81876552d6da8/pythonlib/camoufox/utils.py#L132-L139) function).
However, due to this logic, rarely system using fonts that do not exist on the system, and it seems that we are being blocked by some anti-bot solutions that use font fingerprinting.
Especially in Linux environments, where there are many limitations on font types, having this feature would be particularly useful.

Thank you.

title: Playwright locator.bounding_box() always times out
body:
calls to locator.bounding_box(), locator.screenshot(), locator.evaluate() always time out even though the html element exists & is visible. Other locator methods like locator.text_content(), locator.is_visible(), locator.click() work as expected. Simple proof of concept below:

```
import asyncio
import json
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

# Example config
CONFIG = {
 'window.outerHeight': 1056,
 'window.outerWidth': 1920,
 'window.innerHeight': 1008,
 'window.innerWidth': 1920,
}

async def main():
    async with async_playwright() as p:
        # Create a Firefox instance to the launcher
        browser = await p.firefox.launch(
            # Pass in the Camoufox launcher and config JSON
            executable_path='/path/to/camoufox/launch',
            args=['--config', json.dumps(CONFIG)],
            # Launch in headful mode
            headless=False
        )
        # Continue as normal
        page = await browser.new_page()
        await page.goto('https://example.com')
        await asyncio.sleep(3)
        locator = page.locator("xpath=//h1")
        l1 = locator.first
        print(await l1.count())
        print(await l1.text_content())
        print(await l1.bounding_box())
        await asyncio.sleep(3)
        await browser.close()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```
